item.title: Red Roses' 41-game unbeaten run ended in dramatic fashion
item.description: England's 41-game unbeaten run is over after they were stunned by a late rally from Canada, the Red Roses falling 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto.

item.title: How to Watch: Kansas at K-State
item.description: We just wanted to let you boo Dylan Edwards ahead of time. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Twice in the last three years, the streak appeared to be in jeopardy. Last season, it wasn’t even close. Today, K-State will try and extend their winning streak over Kansas to “voting age”. So naturally, we’re all pretty nervous. The Game The Kansas State Wildcats (3-2, 0-2 Big 12) host the Kansas Jayhawks (2-3, 0-2 Big 12). Kansas leads the all-time series 64-54-5, although officially it’s 63-55-5 because of cheating. Kansas has decided that the Big 8 ruling declaring their 1980 win a forfeit doesn’t matter anymore since there’s no Big 8 anymore. Go figure. But it’s been 17 in a row for the Cats since a three-game KU winning streak in the late 00s. Obviously there’s a lot at stake today, not least the opportunity to avoid an 0-3 start in conference play. It’s a big game. Kansas hasn’t really been competitive against opponents with pulses, but K-State hasn’t really either so there’s another reason for trepidation. Kickoff Saturday, October 17, 11:00am CT at Bill Snyder Family Stadium (50,000) in Manhattan, Kansas. Tickets The game is officially a sellout, with standing-room only tickets avaliable from the ticket office. Via third-party outlets, you’re not getting in the door for under $78 at this writing, and the median price is $122. Weather The good news: the sun will be out, and game-time temps will start in the low 50s anr rise to nearly 60 by game’s end. The bad news? It’ll probably be under 40° when you start your tailgate. Bundle up. Odds Per our friends at DraftKings K-State is a 3.5-point favorite with a 55.5 over. That should translate to a 30-26 K-State win. The money line is -175 for the Cats, +145 for the Jayhawks. Television FS1 with Eric Collins and Spencer Tillman. Radio As always, Wyatt Thompson, Stan Weber, and Matt Walters will be on hand on the K-State Sports Network as well as via satellite on SiriusXM 173 or 237. Internet Streaming The game will stream on FOX Sports (cable, satellite, or internet tv subscription required). Audio available via kstatesports.com . Live stats provided by StatBroadcast . Editorial note: comments are disabled on How to Watch posts to combat illicit streaming spam.

item.title: Chelsea fans’ preferred lineup against Everton: Never change a winning lineup
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 10: Chelsea's Jordan Henderson celebrates scoring his side's fifth goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and AFC Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge on October 10, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images It’s the age-old question. Do you change a winning lineup? Do you play to your strengths as you perceive them, or do you try to anticipate and react to the opponents’ perceived strengths? The answers to those two questions rarely align exactly. As far as the WAGNH Community’s concerned, the correct answer is to stay with what worked last week and what gave us our best performance yet of the young season. This means the midfield pairing of Moisés Caicedo and Jordan Henderson, and the back three of Levi Colwill, Maxence Lacroix, and Josh Acheampong. There should be no doubt about the front-three of course. In fact, it’s only at right wing-back where we get a bit of indecision, but a converted Pedro Neto (55%) still holds off the presumed first-choice in Marco Palestra (41%). The summer signing had impressed in preseason but has been hurt ever since. He did come off the bench last week to make his debut, so presumably his first start for Chelsea isn’t too far behind … but maybe not just yet. 3-4-3 / 3-4-2-1 (75%) Martínez (96%) | Colwill (93%), Lacroix (97%), Acheampong (87%) | Chavarría (81%), Caicedo (99%), Henderson (78%), Neto (55%) | Rogers (99%), Palmer (99%) | João Pedro (97%) Given the dominance of the starters, the rest did not come close to sniffing a starting spot. Roméo Lavia (24%), Estêvão (16%), Jorrel Hato (10%), and Wesley Fofana (10%) at least reached the double digits.

(Photo by Alfredo ESTRELLA / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Pumas got back to the victorious road after defeating Atlante by a 2-1 score. In a lively match, Pumas overcome some defensive mistakes to get victory in more than a month and temporarily climb to 9th place in the Liga MX standings. A cross into the area would be cleared into the path of Jhojan Julio, who got off a right footed shot that forced a good save from Pumas’ goalkeeper, Keylor Navas. Rodrigo Lopez got off a right footed shot from way outside the area that went well wide. A great run by Luis Puente ended with the ball getting to Julio, who got off a right footed that was brilliantly saved by Navas. Because of protesting, the referee would give a red card to Atlante’s coach, Miguel Herrera. A cross into the area was headed by Robert Morales into the path of Juninho, who volleyed the ball from close range past Atlante’s goalkeeper, Oscar Jimenez to score and give Pumas the 1-0 lead. A couple of minutes later, Luis Calzadilla was given time and space to get off a right footed shot in the area that went past Navas to score and tie the match at 1-1. Calzadilla would get off a right footed shot from outside the area that Navas would make another great save off. The 1st half ended as the match was tied in a very lively match. The 2nd half started with neither team making a change so far. Pizzzuto got off a great left footed shot from outside the area that forced another save from Navas. Off a counter, the ball got to Antuna, whose right footed s hot was well saved by Jimenez. Pumas subbed out Alan Medina for Victor Arteaga. A cross into the area was headed well wide by Julio. Atlante subbed out Edgar Jimenez for Diogo Bagui. Off a counter, a great run from Carrasquilla ended with a wonderful pass to Juninho, who got off a left footed shot past Jimenez to score and give Pumas the 2-1 lead. Atlante subbed out Aaron Quiros for Christian Bermudez. A cross into the area was deflected into the path of Pedro Vite, who whiffed on his volley and wasted a chance. A cross into the area was deflected terribly by Ruben Duarte, forcing Navas to make a great save to prevent the own goal. Pumas subbed out Juninho for Alvaro Angulo. Atlante subbed out Eugenio Pizzuto and Eduardo Tercero for Joaquin Moxica and Jairon Charcopa. A longball looked like a good chance for Morales but Jimenez was able to clear the ball before he had a 1 vs 1 chance. Pumas subbed out Uriel Antuna for Santiago Lopez. The time ended and Pumas got a very important result to get back to their winning ways. Pumas got a key victory after defeating Atlante on Friday night. The return of the clash between Mexico City teams had Pumas being at times lucky as although they had a lot of the possession, their defensive mistakes meant that Atlante had a lot of opportunities that goalkeeper Navas prevented from going to the scoreboard. Pumas showed some life at offense, something they had already done in their 3-3 tie on Sunday against Cruz Azul. A couple of dangerous counters by Carrasquilla showed that Pumas is bouncing back on offense but the same can’t be said about defense. Pumas will have another road match midweek when they travel north to face the fast improving Santos. Atlante will also go north as they play their first ever Liga MX match against FC Juarez in Ciudad Juarez on Tuesday.

item.title: “That’s my new nickname” – Angel Reese Embraces CJ McCollum’s Moniker While Praising Hawks Guard’s Support
item.description: Angel Reese © Atlanta Dream/X A couple of days before the WNBA Finals, Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum praised Angel Reese for her impact on the Dream. McCollum even called Reese “the queen of the South.” In a media availability on Friday, Reese, a three-time WNBA All-Star, embraced the nickname. “Shoutout to CJ McCollum. I appreciate the love and support, and I appreciate the support from the Hawks…I guess that’s my new nickname, queen of the South. It’s cool.” McCollum and Reese both came to Atlanta this year. In January, McCollum joined the Hawks via the trade that sent Trae Young to the Washington Wizards. Three months later, the Chicago Sky dealt Reese and a 2028 second-round draft swap to the Dream for two future first-round picks. For both McCollum and Reese, the impact on winning was immediate. McCollum helped the Hawks reach the postseason after back-to-back seasons missing the playoff bus, while Reese (crowned 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year) has been integral to the Dream’s unblemished playoff record heading into the Finals. “She’s Rebuilt Her Shot From Scratch”: Dream Coach Karl Smesko Talks About Helping Angel Reese Fine-Tune Her Shooting Angel Reese’s first season with the Dream also marks Karl Smesko’s second year as the team’s coach. In a media availability on Friday, Smesko talked about spending time with Reese during practice sessions as she worked on her shooting. “I thought it would be a good way for Angel and me to get to know each other a little bit and develop a relationship, if we could spend some time together every day…She’s rebuilt her shot from scratch, from two weeks before the first game of the season, which is just remarkable that you’d even do that at that point.” While Reese isn’t exactly known for her perimeter shooting, she has held her own from beyond the arc in the playoffs. When the Dream went 3-0 in the second round to eliminate the New York Liberty, Reese shot a combined 4-for-7 from deep. item.title: Avalanche’s Jared Bednar makes sobering admission after Penguins win
item.description: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Avalanche’s Jared Bednar makes sobering admission after Penguins win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Colorado Avalanche have had a fantastic start to the 2026-27 NHL season. Colorado is looking to build upon its phenomenal 2025-26 regular season performance. So far, they’ve picked up big wins. But head coach Jared Bednar is happy with simply winning. The Avalanche came away with a big win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday. Colorado needed a rally after a bit of a sluggish start. After the game, Bednar made a tough admission regarding how the team has to continuously claw back into games . “I’m convinced our guys know what makes us successful as a team, but we’re just having a tough time right now putting together a full 60,” Bednar said, via NHL.com. “But when we decide to play and play the right way with the right level of, for me it’s intensity and discipline, then we’re a really good team, and we’re playing well. We just we have to find a way to just get it there for 60 minutes.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Avalanche have not been able to string together wins as of late. As a matter of fact, they haven’t strung together any consistent results. Colorado has alternated wins and losses in each of its last seven games, as NHL.com points out. Colorado fell behind 2-0 in the first period, but was able to storm back after the opening frame. The Avalanche scored five unanswered goals to make it a 5-2 victory at the end of the night. Colorado will need to find a way to start games on time with some consistency. They have a chance to win their second straight on Monday when they face the winless Philadelphia Flyers. Related: Avalanche’s Cale Makar reacts to 1st game since becoming a Dad Related: Avalanche’s Nazem Kadri embracing ‘tricky’ position change in 2026-27

item.title: Valkyries fever sweeps Bay Area ahead of WNBA Finals opener
item.description: The Bay Area is buzzing as the Golden State Valkyries prepare for the biggest game in franchise history. The countdown is on to Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, and after one final practice, the Valkyries say they're eager to take the court Saturday at Ballhalla against the Atlanta Dream. With the anticipation building by the hour, head coach Natalie Nakase says her team is more than ready for the moment. "We feel like caged animals, ready to get there into Ballhalla and play our best four quarters of defense," Nakase said. The Valkyries have stormed into the Finals just two years after joining the league, a remarkable accomplishment that has captured the attention of basketball fans across the country. MORE: Valkyries reach record $100M in annual revenue as world's most valuable women's sports franchise Guard Veronica Burton says the excitement is impossible to ignore. "The anticipation is building, but we're ready to play," Burton said. Nakase credits the team's chemistry and selfless mindset for its rapid rise. "Our players have big hearts. They always want success for their teammates more than for themselves. I think that's rare," she said. Forward Gabby Williams believes staying composed under the bright lights of the championship stage will be key. "Whoever stays the most composed will win," Williams said. MORE: Natalie Nakase's high-energy, hands-on coaching has guided Golden State Valkyries to WNBA Finals The Valkyries are expected to get a major boost from their home crowd. Ballhalla has become one of the toughest venues in the league, with fans creating an electric atmosphere every game. "We want to use Ballhalla to our advantage and get a good start," Williams said. Meanwhile, the Atlanta Dream know exactly what they're walking into. "It's going to be loud in there. There's a lot of excitement, probably some nerves, but I'm excited to be there," Dream guard Naz Hillmon said. With the WNBA championship on the line and the Bay Area basketball spotlight shining bright, all eyes now turn to Ballhalla, where the Valkyries will look to take the first step toward a title on Saturday night. Fans rally behind team ahead of finals Fans across the city are embracing the moment, from bars filled with supporters to elaborate neighborhood displays dedicated to the team. Fans across the city are embracing the moment, from bars filled with supporters to elaborate neighborhood displays dedicated to the team. One of the most visible tributes is "Boohalla," a Halloween-themed Valkyries display in the Inner Richmond District near Third Avenue and Clement Street. With the WNBA championship on the line and the Bay Area basketball spotlight shining bright, all eyes now turn to Ballhalla, where the Valkyries will look to take the first step toward a title on Saturday night. Fans rally behind team ahead of finals Fans across the city are embracing the moment, from bars filled with supporters to elaborate neighborhood displays dedicated to the team. Fans across the city are embracing the moment, from bars filled with supporters to elaborate neighborhood displays dedicated to the team. One of the most visible tributes is "Boohalla," a Halloween-themed Valkyries display in the Inner Richmond District near Third Avenue and Clement Street. Visitor Laura Louie said she was impressed by the attention to detail. "It's amazing," Louie said. "They have everything. They have the flag. They have the whole roster with their Halloween dedicated names." The display was created by San Francisco residents Ainsley Rossitto and Sarah Swig, both season ticket holders and longtime supporters of the Valkyries. "We just love the fan base and the culture of the valkyries," Swig said. "To get to see people walking down the street and get to chit chat with people who are also Val fans has been really fun." Rossitto highlighted one of her favorite parts of the installation. "My favorite is, Natalie. I think we've recreated here as Natalie nacauldron," Rossitto said. "For boohalla and she's really cooking up some strategic plays." The display also includes references to the Valkyries' playoff run. "The sweeping with the aces card is really fun," Swig said. Across town at Mother Bar in the Mission District, fans expressed excitement about the growing visibility of women's sports and the Valkyries' success. "I'm so glad we're finally in an era where women's sports are getting the recognition they deserve. We're so excited," one fan said. Another supporter cheered, "Ballhalla yeah. Valkyries yeah..." Season ticket holder Miki Nakamura said she has been waiting years for a WNBA team in San Francisco. "I've been waiting for a wnba team to be here in San Francisco. I'm beyond excited," Nakamura said. As the Valkyries prepare for their first Finals game, supporters say the team's success has created a strong sense of community throughout the Bay Area. Rossitto and Swig said they plan to be at Chase Center for Game 1. "We'll be at the real Ballhalla," they said. The Valkyries will host the Atlanta Dream on Saturday afternoon at Chase Center. Fans expect the sold-out crowd at "Ballhalla" to provide a significant home-court advantage as the franchise pursues its first WNBA championship. item.title: Three Real Madrid players who could benefit from Vinicius’ four-match suspension
item.description: Three Real Madrid players who could benefit from Vinicius’ four-match suspension Vinicius Jr.’s four-match suspension has created a significant selection dilemma for Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, but it could also give Endrick the opportunity he has been waiting for. With the Brazilian winger beginning his ban against Sevilla , Mourinho will need to find an alternative attacking combination, and the young forward is among those hoping to benefit . Endrick has been pushing for greater involvement in recent weeks, and his decisive contribution to Real Madrid’s dramatic 4-3 comeback against Roma has strengthened his case for more minutes. The suspension to Vinicius now gives Mourinho a reason to reconsider his attacking options, with Yan Diomande and Brahim Diaz also competing for opportunities alongside Kylian Mbappe. Endrick could get his breakthrough Endrick played a key role in Real Madrid’s comeback win over AS Roma. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Endrick’s performance against Roma offered a strong reminder of his determination to make an impact, and Vinicius’ suspension creates an opening at precisely the moment he is looking to convince Mourinho. Although the Brazilian’s natural position is centre-forward, his mobility and ability to attack space could make him a viable option on the right wing. That would allow Mbappe to remain the principal attacking threat through the middle, while giving Endrick an opportunity to influence the game from a different position. The Sevilla fixture will therefore be important for the young forward. With Vinicius unavailable for the first game of his suspension, Endrick has a chance to show that he can contribute from a different position. Diomande offers Mourinho an alternative to Vinicius Diomande could feature on his preferred left-wing role. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) In Vinicius’ position, Diomande could occupy the left wing, with Endrick operating on the opposite side and Mbappe leading the attack. This arrangement would give Real Madrid considerable pace and dribbling ability across both flanks while retaining a central goal threat. Diomande’s one-on-one qualities could help Real Madrid stretch opposing defences, particularly against teams that defend in compact formations. item.title: Liverpool’s crazy £560k-per-week deals, now another £80m?
item.description: Liverpool’s crazy £560k-per-week deals, now another £80m? Liverpool went crazy on £560k-per-week deals. Now they look set to drop another £80m and we're struggling to make sense of it. Liverpool sparked a little bit of controversy this year with two deals that tallied around £560k per week. That was with their midfielder moves - renewing Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai to long-term contracts. It was controversial if only because we're not sure the pair can play together in midfield. It also cast a spotlight on Alexis Mac Allister , who very much did not receive such a contract offer and went public on that fact. The message here is that Liverpool view Gravenberch and Szoboszlai as the future of their midfield. That's really the only way to read contracts that approach £300k per week. At the same time, though, the Reds look set to purchase a new midfielder. So what's going on? The big Alex Scott plan Sky Sports are one of several outlets claiming that Liverpool want Alex Scott. Bournemouth are open to a deal, too, as he's about to enter the final 18 months of his contract there. But the Cherries want £80m. That's an awful lot of money for a midfielder that, given the massive contracts already handed out, Liverpool shouldn't really need. However, they do need him. Or at least, Liverpool need a new midfielder who can bring a bit of control in the middle. It's why we've been big on the idea of signing Lamine Camara or Sergi Altimira. Scott, though, does feel like he's cut from the same cloth as Gravenberch and Szoboszlai. Midfielders who can defend but would much rather push on towards goal and influence the attack. And therein lies the problem. Scott is brilliant and homegrown and undoubtedly a player who could thrive at Liverpool. He just also feels like more of the same - a player who doesn't necessarily move the team on as much as he doubles down on a squad build that isn't really working. So we're not entirely convinced about the plan here. Great player? Absolutely. The right one? Not so sure.

item.title: Barcelona could revive pursuit of 20-year-old Premier League forward in 2027 after two rejected bids
item.description: Barcelona could revive pursuit of 20-year-old Premier League forward in 2027 after two rejected bids Barcelona could return to the pursuit of Eli Junior Kroupi in the summer of 2027 after identifying the Bournemouth striker as a potential long-term option for their attack, claims a report from SPORT . The Catalan club considered the Frenchman last summer as an alternative to Julian Alvarez, but Bournemouth’s valuation and the forward’s injury complicated their plans. Kroupi, 20, is now moving closer to a return after suffering a metatarsal fracture in July. He has resumed on-pitch training following several months of rehabilitation, giving him an opportunity to rebuild his fitness and regain the form that attracted Barcelona’s attention. A future move remains uncertain, however, and Barcelona’s interest will depend on their attacking needs and Kroupi’s performances after returning from injury. Barcelona transfer plans: Why Eli Junior Kroupi attracted interest Barcelona’s sporting management considered Kroupi while exploring options to strengthen the number nine position last summer. Barcelona could revive their interest in Eli Junior Kroupi. (Photo by Eddie Keogh/Getty Images) Alvarez was the priority target, but Atletico Madrid’s reluctance made pursuing the Argentine an entirely different challenge. Kroupi emerged as an alternative after an impressive first Premier League season, and his performances convinced the English club that he was a valuable part of their attacking project. Barcelona submitted two offers for the French striker, but Bournemouth rejected both proposals. The Cherries valued Kroupi at more than €100 million and were unwilling to sell one of their principal attacking threats, making an agreement difficult to reach. Kroupi closes in on return after serious injury Kroupi’s injury in July interrupted his progress and complicated Barcelona’s assessment of their attacking options. However, the forward has now resumed training on the pitch as he approaches the next stage of his recovery. Barcelona had two bids rejected for Eli Junior Kroupi. (Photo by Eddie Keogh/Getty Images) His return will be important not only for Bournemouth but also for any club considering a future move. Regaining match fitness and demonstrating that he can reproduce his previous performances will be essential if Barcelona are to renew their interest. Could Barcelona revisit Kroupi in summer 2027? On that note, Barcelona could reconsider Kroupi in 2027, although there is no guarantee that he will become a priority target. This is because much will depend on the club’s requirements at centre-forward and how their current attacking options perform over the coming months. Hansi Flick has several players contributing to Barcelona’s forward line, including Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, Raphinha, Dani Olmo and Fermin Lopez. Hence, their performances and future transfer plans could influence whether the club needs to invest in another

item.title: Jeremy Jacquet says Iraola has warned Liverpool about one thing in particular ahead of Brentford
item.description: Jeremy Jacquet says Iraola has warned Liverpool about one thing in particular ahead of Brentford Jeremy Jacquet has said that Andoni Iraola has told his Liverpool squad to expect a ‘battle all over the field’ against Brentford on Saturday afternoon. The Reds’ third match in seven days takes them to the Gtech Community Stadium as they seek to inflict a first Premier League defeat of the season on Keith Andrews’ side, who begin the day fourth in the table, one point and five places above the Merseysiders. LFC bounced back from their defeat to Manchester City last weekend by winning 6-3 away to LASK in the Champions League, although the Bees are sure to provide a very stern test for their visitors today. Jacquet: Liverpool can expect a ‘battle’ v Brentford Speaking to liverpoolfc.com ahead of the match in west London, Jacquet knows that he and his teammates can expect a physical contest against Brentford, who won this fixture 3-2 on the Reds’ previous visit just under a year ago. The 21-year-old said: “It’s going to be a big game for us. The manager has already told us that it’s going to be a battle all over the field. However, we’ve been working hard in training, even though time has been a bit short, and we will be ready. “I think that we’ve already shown how we can bounce back over in Austria but now it’s important to get back to winning ways, this time in the Premier League.” (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Jacquet’s physicality could be vital for Liverpool Liverpool’s visit to Brentford last October was a chastening experience, with the Reds dominated in the physical stakes and conceding early to a goal initiated by a long throw-in from Michael Kayode. Fatigue might be a factor today, with Iraola’s team having played twice since the Bees’ most recent outing (2-2 away to Aston Villa last Saturday), and the Basque will be forced into at least one change due to Ryan Gravenberch’s suspension following his red card against Man City . However, in Jacquet we have a centre-back who’s one of the best in the Premier League when it comes to individual duels, as exemplified by statistics from Fotmob comparing him with positional peers in the early weeks of the season. Given the tight turnaround and Brentford’s fine form, today’s match will be an enormous test of character for Liverpool. Steven Gerrard is expecting a share of the spoils , but if the Reds can go one better and emerge with all three points, it’d represent a magnificent victory to round off a busy week and carry strong momentum into upcoming Anfield assignments against Villarreal and Brighton.

item.title: Oklahoma football news: Brent Venables’ contract buyout details after 2-year extension, revealed
item.description: Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Oklahoma football news: Brent Venables’ contract buyout details after 2-year extension, revealed appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma football made a significant financial commitment to Brent Venables , and the cost of firing him has already doubled. The Sooners. signed Venables to a six-year contract extension in August, keeping him under contract through January 2032. The new agreement is worth $63 million, averaging $10.5 million annually. However, its buyout provisions reveal how expensive a coaching change could become. According to George Stoia of On3, Oklahoma would owe Venables approximately $51.67 million if it fired him after the 2026 season. Without the extension, that figure would have been approximately $26.2 million. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The buyout decreases to $41.67 million after 2027 and $31.67 million after 2028. It falls to $21.67 million after 2029 and approximately $5.83 million after 2030. Venables will earn $10 million in 2026, with annual raises of $200,000. His salary reaches $11 million in 2031. The contract also includes performance incentives tied to postseason success. Venables can earn $500,000 for reaching the College Football Playoff, plus additional bonuses for advancing. The financial details emerge during an uneven season for Oklahoma. The Sooners entered October with questions surrounding their offense and Venables’ long-term future. However, Oklahoma recently defeated No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry , securing a 27-24 victory. That result provided a timely boost for Venables following earlier struggles. Oklahoma’s substantial buyout now adds another consideration to any future coaching decision. The extension offers stability, but moving in another direction would carry a high financial cost. For Oklahoma, the extension represents more than a vote of confidence in Venables. It also raises the financial stakes surrounding the program’s future. Sustained success in the SEC could justify that investment, while continued struggles would make any potential coaching change considerably more expensive. Related: Stephen A. item.content:encoded: Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Oklahoma football news: Brent Venables’ contract buyout details after 2-year extension, revealed appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma football made a significant financial commitment to Brent Venables , and the cost of firing him has already doubled. The Sooners. signed Venables to a six-year contract extension in August, keeping him under contract through January 2032. The new agreement is worth $63 million, averaging $10.5 million annually. However, its buyout provisions reveal how expensive a coaching change could become. According to George Stoia of On3, Oklahoma would owe Venables approximately $51.67 million if it fired him after the 2026 season. Without the extension, that figure would have been approximately $26.2 million. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The buyout decreases to $41.67 million after 2027 and $31.67 million after 2028. It falls to $21.67 million after 2029 and approximately $5.83 million after 2030. Venables will earn $10 million in 2026, with annual raises of $200,000. His salary reaches $11 million in 2031. The contract also includes performance incentives tied to postseason success. Venables can earn $500,000 for reaching the College Football Playoff, plus additional bonuses for advancing. The financial details emerge during an uneven season for Oklahoma. The Sooners entered October with questions surrounding their offense and Venables’ long-term future. However, Oklahoma recently defeated No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry , securing a 27-24 victory. That result provided a timely boost for Venables following earlier struggles. Oklahoma’s substantial buyout now adds another consideration to any future coaching decision. The extension offers stability, but moving in another direction would carry a high financial cost. For Oklahoma, the extension represents more than a vote of confidence in Venables. It also raises the financial stakes surrounding the program’s future. Sustained success in the SEC could justify that investment, while continued struggles would make any potential coaching change considerably more expensive. Related: Stephen A. Smith pressures Notre Dame to win out before BYU tilt Related: Washington HC Jedd Fisch gives props to Huskies after wild -4 turnover game vs. Purdue

item.title: “Happiest person in the world”: Man United Women coach Eva Olid reveals what she cannot wait for this season
item.description: “Happiest person in the world”: Man United Women coach Eva Olid reveals what she cannot wait for this season Manchester United Women have turned a corner lately after a rough start under new manager Eva Olid. The Catalan coach has guided her team to four consecutive wins, and they will look to make it five in a row when they face Charlton Athletic away on Sunday afternoon. The BBC sat down with the United coach to pick her brains on the club’s start to the new season. Hard work Olid revealed that she has not had much time to explore the city, as she has been spending most of her time between the training ground and home while preparing for her new role. Joining in the middle of pre-season was never going to be easy, but she explained what message she tried to convey to her players. She stated, “I showed that I’m a person before a coach. I didn’t have time to be aware of where I was. I just went there, be myself trying to transmit to the players how I see football, to work hard, that I’m going to be there for them, that I want to make them better players. Trying to transmit the key messages that I wanted the players to take from the first moment.” Tough first week The Red Devils started the season in horrendous fashion, losing 1-2 to London City Lionesses before being taken apart 0-5 at home by Chelsea. Nonetheless, Olid can see the positives from this hard week. She asserted, “it was a difficult week. There were honest conversations. I took responsibility for a lot of things. I think that was a good starting point for the players. I was confident. It’s crazy to say, I was confident because I knew what the problem was. And when you know the problem, you can change that.” The following week, United played excellently in a 1-1 draw versus Arsenal at the Emirates in a match they probably deserved to win. Olid claimed she was incredibly happy with the team’s performance and said, “when you are in Manchester United, you need to find a way to win. It’s a challenge – how you can win and at the same time develop players and at the same time implement a new style of play. You need to find the balance of all that together. And I think these last weeks, we got to that point.” The new coach is settling into the city but has said that she still needs to find a “100% authentic” Spanish tapas bar in the city and hasn’t been brave enough to try driving on British roads yet. Old Trafford experience Finally, she explained how special it will be when she gets the chance to take her team to play at Old Trafford for the first time. She added, “I came 13 years ago to a game – as a fan of football, and what I remember was amazing. On Saturday I went for second time and they showed me the changing rooms. The day that we play there this season, I will feel the happiest person in the world, like really like a dream.” Man United Women results Featured image by Jess Hornby via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Hearts capable of winning Scottish Premiership admits Martin O’Neill
item.description: Hearts capable of winning Scottish Premiership admits Martin O’Neill Martin O’Neill reckons that Tony Bloom’s ambition of winning the Scottish Premiership within ten years of his investment in Hearts is certainly a strong possibility, in fact the Celtic boss actually reckons it will happen… Cameron Devlin of Heart of Midlothian reacts after conceding a third goal scored by Callum Osmand of Celtic (not pictured) during the Scottishl Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on May 16, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Of course it could – and probably would – have happened last season had it not been for Martin O’Neill returning to the club in early January after Celtic disastrous experiment under Wilfried Nancy , an appointment decision that more that anything else that exposes the Celtic board as charlatans. 16.05.2026 Celtic v Hearts, SPFL Premiership Callum Osmand goal against Hearts to give Celtic a 3-1 lead in the title decider. Photo Kenny Ramsay IMAGO/ News Licensing “I do, yeah, I do. I think their recruitment is really good. I think that what they’ve done has put pressure on Celtic and Rangers. They’re a definite challenge,” the Celtic manager admitted. “They kept going all last season. That was a big, big effort. They kept going and they took it right to the last couple of minutes. Are they capable of doing it? Yeah.” Celtic supporters at Celtic Park for the 2026 title showdown with Hearts. Celtic 3 Hearts 1. Photo Vagelis Georgariou Martin O’Neill added: “I think that they’ve got a certain system in place at this minute, which has been used down at Brighton. They used it there and they’re scouring the European scene for these things. “I thought in the opening game of the season against Aberdeen there might have been just a bit of a hangover from last season. I think they’ve put that to bed and I think they’ve come roaring back. I think they’re capable of winning the league even before that.” Martin O’Neill, Manager of Celtic celebrates his teams third goal scored by Callum Osmand (not pictured) during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on May 16, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) “If you’re looking at it from a neutral viewpoint I think it’s only a great thing for Scottish football, that the O** F*** (sic) is being challenged in a big, big way. Rightly so. So it should be as well. Hearts have taken on that and I think they’re here to stay. “I have a lot of admiration for it. I really do. I have a great admiration for the way they stuck at it last season, the whole way through. Considering that they were up there all that time. You’re up there, you’re looking down, you feel as if ‘oh gosh, could it happen’. They kept it going right to the end. “Okay, so they’ve lost the manager and lost a couple of players as well. But I genuinely feel that they’re a strong challenge. I think that can only be good.” Harry Milne of Heart of Midlothian speaks

item.title: Clippers reportedly re- sign 6-foot-5, high-upside versatile wing just 48 hours after releasing him
item.description: Clippers reportedly re- sign 6-foot-5, high-upside versatile wing just 48 hours after releasing him originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Clippers are among the many teams around the league finalizing their rosters by waiving players. The Clippers have had quite the offseason, to say the least, and are looking to put all the noise behind them and focus on having a successful season. LA has been making roster moves throughout the week. One of those moves was waiving former second-round pick Cam Christie. “The Los Angeles Clippers are waiving Cam Christie, league sources told hoopshype. Christie had a $2.30 million salary guarantee date that was approaching. Christie, who recently turned 21, was the 46th pick of the 2024 NBA Draft and spent the past two seasons with the Clippers," HoopsHype's Michael Scotto wrote. Christie didn't have much of an impact on the Clippers, as he rarely had the opportunity to play meaningful minutes. “Christie was the 46th pick in the 2024 NBA Draft and a guy the Clippers were excited to select with their pick. But in the two seasons he's been with the franchise, he's been unable to make strides large enough to warrant an increase in minutes. Aside from that, there weren't many minutes available to him to play, learn through his mistakes, and develop as the Clippers attempted to compete for a deep playoff run,” ClutchPoints’ Tomar Azarly wrote. However, on Friday, LA decided to bring Christie back on a two-way deal, just 48 hours after he cleared waivers. “The Los Angeles Clippers and Cam Christie have agreed to a two-way deal, agent Kevin Bradbury of LIFT Sports Management told hoopshype. Christie, who recently turned 21, was the 46th pick of the 2024 NBA Draft and spent the past two seasons with the Clippers,” Scotto posted. At first glance, the Clippers' decision to bring Christie back so quickly might seem surprising, but the move makes sense. Christie had been on the standard rookie contract he signed after being drafted, and with the opportunity to sign a two-way deal available after he cleared waivers, both sides agreed to move forward. This allows LA to continue developing Christie while giving him another opportunity to remain with the organization. Spending much-needed time in the G League could help him improve his game and work toward earning a larger role with the Clippers. item.title: Where to watch Grand Valley vs. Ferris State: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Anchor-Bone Classic
item.description: Where to watch Grand Valley vs. Ferris State: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Anchor-Bone Classic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of D2 football's great rivalries takes center stage Saturday as No. 1 Ferris State travels to No. 13 Grand Valley State for the latest edition of the Anchor-Bone Classic. The annual showdown between Michigan neighbors a little over an hour apart always gets the juices flowing, though it's difficult to imagine the Lakers or anyone else finding a way to stop the Bulldogs. The reigning national champions have played only one game this season that was decided by fewer than four touchdowns, a 28-14 victory at Central Washington a month ago. Ferris has won its three games since then by a combined score of 170-6, posting shutouts the last two weeks. Dual-threat QB Wyatt Bower leads the team in rushing and has eight TDs on the ground along with seven through the air. Grand Valley will have an extra chip on its shoulder after absorbing an overtime loss last weekend at Michigan Tech, which is now ranked No. 14 in D2. The Lakers saw a fourth-quarter lead slip away in the final minutes and came up empty in OT, leaving them at 5-1 this season. QB Andrew Schuster (1,418 yards, 20 TDs, one interception) is the man to watch as GVSU tries to bounce back. Can the Lakers pull the upset in a rivalry game? Here's all you need to know to watch. Where to watch Grand Valley vs. Ferris State TV channel: None Live stream: FloCollege The Anchor-Bone Classic won't air on traditional television but can be streamed live on FloCollege. New subscribers can get a 15 percent discount on a FloCollege annual subscription through The Sporting News' exclusive offer. Purchasing a FloCollege subscription gives sports fans access to live streams, event replays and FloSports Originals. Grand Valley vs. Ferris State start time Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 3 p.m. ET The Anchor-Bone Classic will kick off Saturday at 3 p.m. ET. The game will be played at Lubbers Stadium in Allendale, Michigan. item.title: Bundesliga centurion Atubolu applauds Frankfurt fans and Koch after first home win
item.description: Bundesliga centurion Atubolu applauds Frankfurt fans and Koch after first home win Noah Atubolu kept his first clean sheet in Eintracht Frankfurt colors as the Eagles finally ended their winless home run on Friday with a 1-0 victory over Köln. The ex-Freiburg shot-stopper conceded 16 goals in his first five games, including a 2-2 draw with his former club. “I'm very relieved and happy that we won. It felt really good,” Atubolu said after his 100th Bundesliga appearance. “The first home win of the season. And, for me, the first home win in an Eintracht jersey. Köln had a great chance early on, but overall we were very solid.” Marius Bülter came close to score within the first minute, but the visitors failed to keep that up for the rest of the game. Despite his costly mistakes in some of their defeats, including last week's game in Leipzig, Atubolu played well in both of their victories. The 24-year-old saved his sixth consecutive penalty-kick when Frankfurt won 3-1 in Mainz on matchday 3. “We defended well together. Everything doesn't always have to be perfect in football. Not everything went smoothly, but if we play so compactly and maturely, we can get a lot of points. We have a lot of quality in attack and we know we're always good for goals. But the focus also has to be on defense, and Robin Koch deserves special mention there. He had a tough week, but played an incredible game. He's a leader, he led from the front and cleared everything away.” Frankfurt’s coach Adi Hütter also praised his captain for his performance after a difficult week for both him and the club. In addition, Atubolu applauded Frankfurt fans for standing with the players and coach after the game in Leipzig. “In Leipzig, the fans had every reason to be angry with us, but they applauded after the game. At that moment I thought to myself: ‘Wow, what a club!’ And it continued today. They pushed us for the full 90 minutes. The fans were one of the reasons why we were able to pull off this gritty victory.” Frankfurt will face Borussia Dortmund in Topspiel action on matchday 7. They will then clash HSV in two competitions, including their cup tie at Volksparkstadion on October 27th.

item.title: Bruins goalie matches Tim Thomas with career first feat vs. Ducks
item.description: Kyle Ross-Imagn Images Bruins goalie matches Tim Thomas with career first feat vs. Ducks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins are having a nice start to the 2026-27 season. Boston made some big offseason moves to maintain their status as a playoff team. On Friday night, they showed that they can stand tall against quality teams. Goalie Michael DiPietro was among the standouts in this contest. The Boston netminder stopped 25 of the 27 shots he faced in this game. He received a huge offensive contribution at the other end of the ice, as well. In the end, the Bruins won 4-2, moving to 6-2-0 on the season. DiPietro’s win was notable as well. The 27-year-old won his first career NHL game. Furthermore, he became the second Bruins goalie in the last 48 years to win his first game at age 27 or older, according to NHL Public Relations. The other netminder to achieve that feat was Tim Thomas. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) DiPietro has had limited experience in the NHL prior to this season. In fact, this is the first time the 27-year-old has appeared in more than a single game in any one season. This was just the fourth career start for the former third-round pick. The Bruins netminder was initially drafted by the Vancouver Canucks in 2017. He appeared in three games for them from 2018-19 to 2021-22. It wasn’t until the 2025-26 campaign that he saw NHL action again. DiPietro is now fully established as the Bruins backup goaltender. He will be the one stepping up when starting netminder Jeremy Swayman is getting a night off. So far, he has shown the ability to stand tall when his team needs him. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins are having a nice start to the 2026-27 season. Boston made some big offseason moves to maintain their status as a playoff team. On Friday night, they showed that they can stand tall against quality teams. Goalie Michael DiPietro was among the standouts in this contest. The Boston netminder stopped 25 of the 27 shots he faced in this game. He received a huge offensive contribution at the other end of the ice, as well. In the end, the Bruins won 4-2, moving to 6-2-0 on the season. DiPietro’s win was notable as well. The 27-year-old won his first career NHL game. Furthermore, he became the second Bruins goalie in the last 48 years to win his first game at age 27 or older, according to NHL Public Relations. In fact, this is the first time the 27-year-old has appeared in more than a single game in any one season. This was just the fourth career start for the former third-round pick. item.description: 1 Cavs player in danger of losing starting job in 2026-27 training camp appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Cavaliers , at the very least, got over the Conference Finals hump during their postseason run in 2026. The problem, of course, was that the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks swept them . There remains plenty of urgency for the Cavs to find a breakthrough, especially after they traded away Darius Garland for James Harden, and their moves this offseason show that the front office is all-in on this core of theirs. Throughout the Donovan Mitchell era, the three-spot has been a bit of a hole for the Cavs. They have tried to deploy Isaac Okoro, Max Strus, and De’Andre Hunter to fill that void, but none of them have stuck. Of those players, Strus did the best job as a rugged defender and movement shooter, but Cleveland knew that this was a position they needed to upgrade in. Considering that the Cavs were in second apron hell not too long ago, it’s quite remarkable of them to pull off a sign-and-trade for up-and-coming combo forward Peyton Watson — giving them a long-term solution at a position of need. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With that said, it doesn’t appear as though any Cavs player is in danger of losing a starting spot heading into the 2026-27 campaign. Peyton Watson is the nailed-on starter for the Cavs at the three 18 different players started at least one game for the Cavs last season. Even Evan Mobley came off the bench on two occasions. But this is a team that has prioritized continuity, and as long as they’re healthy, there will not be much movement in the starting lineup. There’s no reason to expect head coach Kenny Atkinson to make many changes, if any at all, to his starting lineup. Their All-Star backcourt of Mitchell and Harden remains, and their frontcourt is set with Mobley and Jarrett Allen running it back for the sixth consecutive season. Prior to the signing of Watson, it would have been interesting to see who the Cavs would have started in an alternative universe where the Denver Nuggets bit the second apron bullet. Perhaps Cleveland would have started Strus regularly yet again, or maybe new signing Mario Hezonja , after impressing in the EuroLeague, could make his case for a spot in the starting five. But the Cavs did not trade away a 2031 first-round pick, one of their few tradeable draft assets, and sign Watson to a four-year, $88 million contract to have him come off the bench. Watson was making plenty of strides on offense in the middle of the 2025-26 season; amid the Nuggets’ injury woes, there was a stretch from December 22 until February 4 where Watson nailed a starting role and was incredible on a nightly basis. During that aforementioned stretch, Watson averaged 19.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.2 steals, and 1.3 blocks on 49/43/73 shooting splits. Nikola Jokic did miss 16 of the Nuggets’ 25 games during that stretch

The Cleveland Cavaliers , at the very least, got over the Conference Finals hump during their postseason run in 2026. The problem, of course, was that the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks swept them . Throughout the Donovan Mitchell era, the three-spot has been a bit of a hole for the Cavs. They have tried to deploy Isaac Okoro, Max Strus, and De’Andre Hunter to fill that void, but none of them have stuck. Of those players, Strus did the best job as a rugged defender and movement shooter, but Cleveland knew that this was a position they needed to upgrade in. Considering that the Cavs were in second apron hell not too long ago, it’s quite remarkable of them to pull off a sign-and-trade for up-and-coming combo forward Peyton Watson — giving them a long-term solution at a position of need. Peyton Watson is the nailed-on starter for the Cavs at the three 18 different players started at least one game for the Cavs last season. Even Evan Mobley came off the bench on two occasions. But this is a team that has prioritized continuity, and as long as they’re healthy, there will not be much movement in the starting lineup. There’s no reason to expect head coach Kenny Atkinson to make many changes, if any at all, to his starting lineup. Their All-Star backcourt of Mitchell and Harden remains, and their frontcourt is set with Mobley and Jarrett Allen running it back for the sixth consecutive season. Prior to the signing of Watson, it would have been interesting to see who the Cavs would have started in an alternative universe where the Denver Nuggets bit the second apron bullet. Perhaps Cleveland would have started Strus regularly yet again, or maybe new signing Mario Hezonja , after impressing in the EuroLeague, could make his case for a spot in the starting five. But the Cavs did not trade away a 2031 first-round pick, one of their few tradeable draft assets, and sign Watson to a four-year, $88 million contract to have him come off the bench. Watson was making plenty of strides on offense in the middle of the 2025-26 season; amid the Nuggets’ injury woes, there was a stretch from December 22 until February 4 where Watson nailed a starting role and was incredible on a nightly basis. During that aforementioned stretch, Watson averaged 19.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.2 steals, and 1.3 blocks on 49/43/73 shooting splits. Nikola Jokic did miss 16 of the Nuggets’ 25 games during that stretch, which, without a doubt, helped inflate Watson’s stats. But it’s a testament to his improved skill level that he was able to put up those stats while receiving more defensive attention and less help from his three-time MVP teammate. The Cavs won’t have the usage opening for Watson to fill the stat sheet the way he did during that eye-opening stretch. But that doesn’t mean that they aren’t all-in on him as a member of this core. Not only can he wreak havoc defensively, he was much-improved from beyond the arc as well (41.1% last season), making him a valuable off-ball weapon for Harden and Mitchell to feed. Moreover, Watson’s improved game off the bounce means that defenses simply cannot ignore him or close out on him hard. This makes it so that none of the Cavs’ starters are actually under much of a threat to lose their spot. What’s more interesting to monitor is how the Cavs will divvy up the minutes off the bench. Who will be the fixtures off the bench for Kenny Atkinson? Without a doubt, Jaylon Tyson and Sam Merrill will be featuring prominently in the Cavs’ rotation. Merrill can pick up opposing guards for 94 feet, while Tyson impressed as a glue-guy last season , averaging 13.2 points per game while making two triples per game on a 44.6% clip. Hezonja should also be one of the first guys off the bench for Atkinson. Last season, in 66 games across EuroLeague and Liga ACB, Hezonja averaged nearly 15 points per contest on 44/33/87 shooting splits. He can be a huge weapon in transition, and he also provides some defensive tenacity on the wing. Nae’Qwan Tomlin, the team’s resident dirty work guy, Thomas Bryant, the veteran backup big, and Craig Porter Jr. should also get some minutes here and there. Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas may not be in the rotation every night, but they should get some chances to impress and earn minutes. item.description: ROME, ITALY - OCTOBER 14: Endrick of Real Madrid celebrates after scoring a goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AS Roma and Real Madrid C.F. at Stadio Olimpico on October 14, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Danilo Di Giovanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Daily Merengue — a place where you can feel free to discuss all things football. Do not be alarmed by the overt RMCF bias. It’s in the name! Shoutout to the Mods who do a fantastic job, Valyrian Steel, Ezek XI, KungFuZizou, NeRObutBlanco, Felipejack, and Juninho. Writer’s Prelude. We’ll keep is short. Relief A Renewal. According to two sources that I rarely ever trust AS and Fabrizio Romano, but partially confirmed by sources I actually believe carry journalistic credibility, it appears that Jude Bellingham is on the verge of renewing his contract with Real Madrid. Rumor has it that he will be given a salary and stature similar to Vini but exceeding Vini’s as far as it comes to marketing benefits and bonuses. Despite my DT yesterday regarding Jude and his role on the squad, renewing him just simply makes sense especially at this time frame. Jude is the 2nd face of Real Madrid (after Kylian Mbappe) and is one of the most marketable players in the world. He is also arguably our 2nd best player and potentially our most complete player as well. This renewal just simply makes sense and provides the club some leverage in future initiatives. 🚨💣 CONFIRMED: Real Madrid have reached a VERBAL AGREEMENT with Jude Bellingham over a NEW CONTRACT! Formalities will be completed in the coming weeks. @FabrizioRomano pic.twitter.com/njT05HKAWF — Madrid Xtra (@MadridXtra) October 17, 2026 Return . It seem like Eder Militia is finally returning back to the Real Madrid squad. I’ll admit I don’t have supremely high hopes for him but if he can return after his latest injury to even close to his past performance it will be a major boon to our backline depth. Personally, I believe Dean Huijsen has made a significant leap thus far this year, and Konate has reestablished his past self. Militao will face plenty of competition for a starting role but we can only cheer him on and hope for a successful return. Next up Ferland Mendy…and Rodrygo Goes. 🚨💣 BREAKING: Éder Militão is expected to be CALLED UP vs Sevilla on Sunday. @Rodra10_97 🇧🇷 pic.twitter.com/V5RKlHd9F5 — Madrid Xtra (@MadridXtra) October 16, 2026 Renewed Faith. Like clockwork, Endrick’s performance has reached the news cycle with the club reestablishing their faith in the wonderkid. I’m still a bit skeptical on whether it makes sense to keep Endrick this entire season (for his own career) but the upcoming La Liga matches and potentially CL (depending on if Mourinho still chooses to play Vini) will give Endrick his first real chance and best opportunity to establish himself as part of the Real Madrid XI / rotation. item.title: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL’s ‘Next Great’ Cornerback
item.description: The Washington Commanders are "likely" changing the role of second-year cornerback Trey Amos. Getty The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn’t been available for quite some time. Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions. Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he’ll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. “SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!” DC News Now’s Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. “ Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week.” Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that’s taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. “Trey Amos has no hobbies,” Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. “No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back.” Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it’s been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. “My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it’s nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik’s been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside,” The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. Amos started training camp on the PUP list but returned to practice a few weeks later … and automatically got hurt again. “Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day,” The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. “Quinn said he’ll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return.” Trey Amos Called NFL’s ‘Next Great Cornerback’ Pro Football Focus NFL reporter Bradley Locker named Amos to his 2026 NFL All-Breakout Team — his list of the NFL’s “Next Great” players at every position. “Last year’s second-round selection didn’t enjoy the kind of rookie showcase he desi

item.title: Hockey legends back on the ice to mark anniversary
item.description: Steve Nell said there are "not many clubs in the UK that have done 40 years" [BBC] Ice hockey legends who have not skated in years are taking on the Swindon Wildcats team, to mark 40 years of ice hockey in the town. The Wildcats, Wiltshire's only ice hockey team, was founded in 1986 by five players from the North East shortly after the opening of the town's Link Centre. To mark the club's 40th anniversary, a team of former players are lacing up their skates again to face the current 2026/27 roster in a "one-of-a-kind" match on Saturday. Steve Nell, managing director, said: "When I asked [the legends], everybody was: 'yes'. Now some of them are out there and it's a little bit tougher - [they're] stiff and haven't skated for a long time but everybody will be fine on the day." More from Wiltshire 'Collapsed bridge findings' and 'Animal cruelty' 'Menace' driver tried to bite officers after chase Delight as footbridge saved after community outcry The Wildcats play in the National Ice Hockey League (NIHL) and are the current reigning champions. Nell said he was playing ice hockey in Sunderland when he and four others "got the opportunity" to move to Swindon in the 1980s and set up the team. "There's not many clubs in the UK that have done 40 years," he said. "The [players] have been a big part of the club over the years and there's still some people watching from the first year. "It's such a big anniversary. I just think it's important to celebrate." Daryl Lipsey says he hopes the fans "aren't expecting" him to be as good as he used to be [BBC] Daryl Lipsey, who was also one of the original founding players, said it had been years since he pulled on the kit but it was "nice to come back". "The last time I played on the ice was 10 years ago, when we did the last legends game," he said. "So it's been a long time." For the anniversary match, he will not only be taking to the ice for the first time in a decade but going head-to-head with his two sons, who are on the Wildcats team. "I just hope the fans aren't expecting me to be as good as I used to be," he said. "But I'm looking forward to it. It will be fun." Richard Howe said he will "mainly be focussed" on staying on his feet [BBC] Richard Howe, who played for the side in the 1980s and early 1990s, said it was going to "feel great" stepping out on to the ice in front of a packed Link Centre but he will "mainly be focussed" on staying on his feet. "The first [training session] was pretty shaky - the second one was definitely better but I should be alright on Saturday," he said. "I'm looking forward to getting back out in front of the crowd again. "The hockey is probably of a higher standard but the crowd, the building, the changing room - it's all the same." item.title: NASCAR Truck Championship Battle Becomes More Clear After Phoenix
item.description: NASCAR Truck Series championship battle becomes more clear after Phoenix. Getty Kaden Honeycutt expanded his points lead in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series following a win at Phoenix. The driver of the No. 11 drove to victory in Friday night’s Zero Carbon Bioethanol 150 at the 1.0-mile Arizona track, extending his lead over Layne Riggs to 39 points. With three races remaining in the 2026 season, Riggs, who entered the Chase as the top seed, finds himself working from behind. The driver of the No. 34 had a strong third-place run in the desert, but it was not enough to keep Honeycutt from widening the points gap. At this juncture, the Truck Series championship is seemingly down to two drivers. Although no drivers have been mathematically eliminated, every Chase driver except Riggs faces a 100-plus points deficit with only three races left. Christian Eckes ranks third in the standings after Phoenix but is 112 points behind leader Honeycutt. Chandler Smith, a two-time winner this season, sits fourth in the standings, 117 points out of the lead. item.content:encoded: NASCAR Truck Series championship battle becomes more clear after Phoenix. Getty Kaden Honeycutt expanded his points lead in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series following a win at Phoenix. The driver of the No. 11 drove to victory in Friday night’s Zero Carbon Bioethanol 150 at the 1.0-mile Arizona track, extending his lead over Layne Riggs to 39 points. With three races remaining in the 2026 season, Riggs, who entered the Chase as the top seed, finds himself working from behind. The driver of the No. 34 had a strong third-place run in the desert, but it was not enough to keep Honeycutt from widening the points gap. At this juncture, the Truck Series championship is seemingly down to two drivers. Although no drivers have been mathematically eliminated, every Chase driver except Riggs faces a 100-plus points deficit with only three races left. Christian Eckes ranks third in the standings after Phoenix but is 112 points behind leader Honeycutt. Chandler Smith, a two-time winner this season, sits fourth in the standings, 117 points out of the lead. item.title: A major challenge looms on the horizon for Manchester City and Enzo Maresca
item.description: A major challenge looms on the horizon for Manchester City and Enzo Maresca Manchester City have made a strong start to the 2026-27 season. Prior to their 4-2 loss to PSG , Enzo Maresca’s side had won eight consecutive matches in all competitions. It is clear to see that this new-look City side is beginning to click and grow together. However, due to the heavy fixture list and the importance of every match in the Premier League and UEFA Champions League, it is difficult for Enzo Maresca to provide his key players with the rest that they need. But rest for Manchester City’s most important players is required at times so it is a major problem that Enzo Maresca had acknowledged. Enzo Maresca knows that he will have to rest key players throughout the season. Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledged that Erling Haaland will need to be rested at some point in the near future. Haaland has carried a heavy workload for both club and country this season. Also, Haaland had a busy summer with Norway at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, like many of his teammates. Maresca added it wasn’t just Haaland who will need to be rested on occasions this season. He explained, when talking to the media yesterday , ahead of Manchester City’s upcoming Premier League fixture against Ipswich Town: “ At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off. ” “ We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams. “ “ Elliot, Enzo, Marc, Erling, Rúben – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest .” Manchester City do have depth in their squad which will be needed. Juggling the fitness and fatigue of key players is an issue that Enzo Maresca will have to confront throughout his first season as Manchester City’s manager. Off the back of a busy summer for a host of City’s players, a close eye will have to be kept on the players’ fatigue levels. There is no doubt that this will occur and is already in progress now. It will be an ongoing process throughout this season. What Manchester City will not want is to lose key players such as Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Marc Guehi, Ruben Dias and others for extended periods. To avoid this, Enzo Maresca will have to rotate his squad throughout the season. Fortunately, City do have the necessary squad depth to do this. Enzo Maresca will have to utilise his entire squad throughout the season. There isn’t an ideal period for Maresca to rest key players. Manchester City’s fixture list is relentless and there are no easy games. Instead, Maresca will have to trust his squad and continue to use clever substitutions as he has already this season. That will be a juggling act for Maresca, but it is one he is capable of putting together. Enzo Maresca is fully aware that he will have to rest key players such as Erling Haaland throughout the season. That cannot be avoided. Lucki

item.title: “Worst GM in the NFL” “Failure of a move”: Fans Slam Colts FO For Releasing Darius Slayton 24 Days After Free Agent Move
item.description: Darius Slayton © Instagram/@sl1msl8y Just 24 days after signing with the Indianapolis Colts as a free agent, wide receiver Darius Slayton was released on Friday without playing a single game. The veteran wideout, who played for the New York Giants from 2019 through 2025, signed with the Colts on Sept. 22 but was released after reportedly struggling to learn the offense. Slayton’s release from the Colts hasn’t sat right with fans online, with many calling out the franchise’s front office and general manager Chris Ballard. “Ballard is the worst GM in the NFL…. PERIOD,” wrote a fan on X. “What a failure of a move: Slayton played zero snaps for the Colts,” commented a fan on X. With the 2026 regular NFL season now in its sixth week, the Indianapolis Colts sit in second in the AFC South standings with a 2-3 record. Shane Steichen Reveals Why Colts Released Darius Slayton Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen opened up about the veteran wideout’s abrupt departure from the franchise. In a press conference on Friday, Steichen acknowledged Slayton’s efforts in practice, but said the move simply did not work out as expected. “He had some good weeks of practice, unfortunately, it just didn’t work out and I think those happen. I got a lot of respect for him, what he’s done in this league, and I wish him the best going forward.” Slayton did not play a single snap for the Colts. He was sidelined for the Week 5 game against the Steelers with a knee injury. item.description: SANTA CLARA, CA - DECEMBER 23: Khalil Mack #52 of the Chicago Bears rushes the quarterback against the San Francisco 49ers during their NFL game at Levi's Stadium on December 23, 2018 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Robert Reiners/Getty Images) | Getty Images 49ers injury updates: Kyle Juszczyk practices in full; 2 rookies miss “Wide receiver Mike Evans didn’t practice for the second day in a row. This is likely how it’ll be with Evans this year. Even if he doesn’t practice, he’ll still suit up on game day. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton missed a second straight day with a quad injury. That’s suboptimal, given the injuries at the position. The 49ers are as thin as you can be at the position. The silver lining is that James Thompson was listed as limited, although that’s not a 1-for-1 swap. Rookie Romello Height was a new addition after practicing in full on Thursday. Height’s designation is an illness, so the hope is that he’s fine, with the game still 72 hours away.” 49ers’ John Lynch says he’s shopping before NFL trade deadline; Kittle asks about Khalil Mack (paywall) “When asked on KNBR on Friday morning about the 49ers possibly trading for Mack, 35, Lynch said “a lot of people ask me that” before revealing Kittle posed the question Thursday. “It’s usually Kittle because he asks about everything, which I love,” Lynch said….“I just like to chirp him and ask what he’s interested in and see if he’ll give me anything,” Kittle said. “So he didn’t really give me a lot yesterday. But me, (fullback Kyle Juszczyk), (left tackle) Trent (Williams), we’ll chirp him just to see if he’ll actually tell us anything. I think he tells Trent the most. Not me, though.” Examining the 49ers’ early-season feat: Generating pressure without Nick Bosa (paywall) “This year, Osa Odighizuwa already has 15 pressures after just five games while rookie Gracen Halton has seven. (Photo by Robert Reiners/Getty Images) | Getty Images 49ers injury updates: Kyle Juszczyk practices in full; 2 rookies miss “Wide receiver Mike Evans didn’t practice for the second day in a row. This is likely how it’ll be with Evans this year. Even if he doesn’t practice, he’ll still suit up on game day. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton missed a second straight day with a quad injury. Height’s designation is an illness, so the hope is that he’s fine, with the game still 72 hours away.” 49ers’ John Lynch says he’s shopping before NFL trade deadline; Kittle asks about Khalil Mack (paywall) “When asked on KNBR on Friday morning about the 49ers possibly trading for Mack, 35, Lynch said “a lot of people ask me that” before revealing Kittle posed the question Thursday. “It’s usually Kittle because he asks about everything, which I love,” Lynch said….“I just like to chirp him and ask what he’s interested in and see if he’ll give me anything,” Kittle said. “So he didn’t really give me a lot yesterday. But me, (fullback Kyle Juszczyk), (left tackle) Trent (Williams), we’ll chirp him just to see if he’ll actually tell us anything. I think he tells Trent the most. Not me, though.” Examining the 49ers’ early-season feat: Generating pressure without Nick Bosa (paywall) “This year, Osa Odighizuwa already has 15 pressures after just five games while rookie Gracen Halton has seven. Odighizuwa’s 12.8 percent pass rush win rate ranks 12th at his position among those who have played five games. Halton’s is 9.6 percent, a rate Odighizuwa says ought to climb as Halton, a fourth-round pick, continues to improve his technique. Halton missed Thursday’s practice with a quadriceps injury. “He’s very raw now,” Odighizuwa said. “So you’re just seeing nothing but upside when you’re watching him play. So it’s exciting stuff.” John Lynch states 49ers trade discussions have ramped up ahead of deadline “Just because the flow of the trade deadline is approaching, yes,” he said. “That’s our job to do that, to talk with our counterparts around the league. We receive calls, we make calls, just to see where the market is at.” Raheem Morris, Klay Kubiak, Brock Purdy share updates ahead of 49ers-Commanders “It was a lot of fun. I’ll give you a quick story. I remember people asking me, ‘How was it coaching [former NFL WR] Julio Jones?’ I said, ‘It’s easy. Good catch, Julio’ (laughter). No, all joking aside, you were able to take your defensive analysis and bring it to those guys while you were learning how to be a good offensive coach and the detail and everything that’s required. That goes into scoring touchdowns and staying on the field and manufacturing first downs. Being around Kyle that first year on offense, it was really the philosophy of what we’re trying to do on football games and how we’re going to go out there and attack people. I had so much fun being able to be over there with the likes of Kyle Shanahan, [Green Bay Packers head coach] Matt LaFleur, [Arizona Cardinals head coach] Mike LaFleur was on that staff, [Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator] Mike McDaniel. It was a bunch of really great coaches that were teaching me the backend. And in the frontend, you had all the guys on the front end like [assistant head coach/offensive line coach] Chris Foerster and those guys just teaching you what it was like in the run game and what the rules were and everything that was required to go out there and accomplish what we wanted to get accomplished. You can’t help but bring that back to defense when you had to go back over there. So, when I was able to go back and really formulate how I see the game, how I feel the game, how you want to make your players feel the game, that philosophy really helped me a lot to grow. I think everything from the beginning was really helpful for me when it came to offensive football.” 49ers Week 5 Trench Grades: The duality of it all (paywall) “This week was defined by Gracen Halton dominating and Connor Colby getting dominated. After an encouraging start, Colby is officially a problem. Seattle attacked him, and what’s particularly cool is that I was able to really track that effectively. Because I logged Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams as elite players (same for Demarcus Lawrence in the run game), we were able to identify that Seattle got Colby isolated against one of that elite pairing consistently. And he consistently lost. It’s one of the cooler reflections of tape to data thus far this season…..Keion White was a menace, and Romello Height is very clearly starting to cook, club and all. Mykel Williams also had a basic bull rush pressure that became White’s sack. It’s worth noting that Williams exclusively played on the edge this week. That’s easing him back into it. I would be stunned if that doesn’t change as the season goes.”

item.title: “I Don’t Care Who Starts Just Win”: Fans React As Florida Reportedly Set to Start New QB vs Arch Manning’s Texas After Injury to Aaron Philo
item.description: Tramell Jones © @tramelljonesjr/Instagram The Florida Gators are expected to start quarterback Tramell Jones against Arch Manning’s Texas on Saturday. Quarterback Aaron Philo is recovering from a shoulder injury, and Pete Nakos reported that Florida will turn to Jones. Florida fans were quick to react to the news. “Let’s go I don’t care who starts just win,” one fan said . Philo suffered a shoulder injury in the fourth quarter during Florida’s blowout loss to South Carolina. Jon Sumrall talks about QB troubles Philo’s status is still questionable, and the final decision will be made on Saturday. Florida head coach Jon Sumrall talked about backup quarterback Tramell Jones. “Tramell got reps in practice. He’s going to continue to get reps. I’ve said this publicly, I think Tramell can be our starting quarterback here, and we can win football games,” Sumrall told reporters earlier this week . “Tramell is gonna be ready when his number is called, and he’s gonna continue to have opportunities as we move forward. I love the way he’s handled himself. Tramell’s been great. Philo’s been great,” he added.
