item.title: Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor downgraded for LSU clash
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor downgraded for LSU clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor, who is dealing with a turf toe injury , has been downgraded to doubtful and is not expected to play on Saturday against LSU, according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel. The sophomore was listed as questionable on Wednesday and Thursday before his status changed Friday. Taylor sustained the injury during the Bulldogs’ September 26 win over Missouri and continued playing through the pain in the team’s October 3 loss to Alabama. He eventually left the 56-23 defeat in the fourth quarter and was later seen wearing a boot on his right foot. Through five games, Taylor has completed 102 of 154 passes, recording 1,450 passing yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed 43 times for 159 yards and a touchdown. His performances had placed him among the Heisman Trophy contenders before Mississippi State suffered its first loss of the season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) If Taylor cannot play, the Bulldogs are expected to start true freshman Parker “Billy” Puckett. The backup quarterback completed three of six passes for 26 yards after entering against the Crimson Tide. Across the season, Puckett has completed eight of 14 attempts for 89 yards and rushed twice for 24 yards. Redshirt freshman Puckett is listed as the No. 2 quarterback, while fifth-year senior AJ Swann and former Florida quarterback Jaden Rashada provide additional options. Mississippi State could also be without its leading running back, Fluff Bothwell, who was downgraded to doubtful on Friday because of a lower-body injury. Bothwell has racked up 403 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 74 carries, making his potential absence another concern for the Bulldogs’ offense. The matchup carries considerable implications for both teams. No. 16 Mississippi State enters at 4-2 overall and 2-1 in SEC play, while No. 22 Tigers are also 4-2 but holds a 1-2 conference record. Kickoff is scheduled for for 12 p.m. ET in Baton Rouge, with ESPN broadcasting the game. Related: Stephen A. Smith pressures Notre Dame to win out before BYU tilt Related: Washington HC Jedd Fisch gives props to Huskies after wild -4 turnover game vs. Purdue

item.title: Barcelona team news: Hansi Flick considering major rotations against Real Betis
item.description: Barcelona team news: Hansi Flick considering major rotations against Real Betis As per SPORT , Barcelona manager Hansi Flick is preparing to rotate his starting XI against Real Betis as he manages his squad ahead of crucial fixtures against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid. Following the demanding Champions League encounter against Galatasaray, Flick will have to balance the team to compete for three points in La Liga with keeping his key players fresh for the trips and challenges ahead. On that note, the outlet points out that Jules Kounde and Xavi Espart are candidates to start in defence, while Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus could also feature from the beginning. Barcelona’s match against Betis is the first of three demanding fixtures, with PSG up next before the meeting with Real Madrid. Flick’s selection will therefore be important in managing workloads without sacrificing the team’s attacking threat or defensive stability. Kounde and Espart could start against Betis Jules Kounde will replace Eric Garcia on the right. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images) Kounde and Xavi Espart are among the players in contention to enter the starting XI after beginning the Galatasaray match on the bench. Kounde could occupy the right-back position, with Espart potentially starting on the left. Their inclusion would allow Flick to manage the minutes of Joao Cancelo and Eric Garcia, who could be needed for the subsequent Champions League fixture against PSG. Flick faces midfield dilemma with Rodri, Pedri and Fermin The midfield presents a more complicated decision, as Flick has been reluctant to leave Rodri out of his starting XI, instead managing the midfielder’s workload without necessarily substituting him before the final whistle. Frenkie de Jong’s return gives the manager another option, with Marc Bernal and Gavi also available to compete for places. Gavi could find a place in the starting XI agianst Real Betis. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Pedri and Fermin Lopez are candidates to retain their positions after starting against Galatasaray, although Gavi could enter the team and displace one of them. With several players capable of filling different roles, the Barcelona manager must decide where rotation is most practical without weakening the team’s control in midfield. Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus could lead Barcelona attack As expected, Lamine Yamal is expected to retain his place in the starting XI, while Adeyemi could replace Anthony Gordon after making an impact off the bench against Galatasaray. The German forward’s goal in Istanbul strengthens his case for a starting opportunity against Betis. Gabriel Jesus is another potential change. Having started the Champions League fixture on the bench, the Brazilian is in contention to lead the line as Barcelona look to maintain their attacking threat while managing minutes across the squad.

Frenkie de Jong’s return gives the manager another option, with Marc Bernal and Gavi also available to compete for places. Gavi could find a place in the starting XI agianst Real Betis. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Pedri and Fermin Lopez are candidates to retain their positions after starting against Galatasaray, although Gavi could enter the team and displace one of them. With several players capable of filling different roles, the Barcelona manager must decide where rotation is most practical without weakening the team’s control in midfield. Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus could lead Barcelona attack As expected, Lamine Yamal is expected to retain his place in the starting XI, while Adeyemi could replace Anthony Gordon after making an impact off the bench against Galatasaray. The German forward’s goal in Istanbul strengthens his case for a starting opportunity against Betis. Gabriel Jesus is another potential change. Having started the Champions League fixture on the bench, the Brazilian is in contention to lead the line as Barcelona look to maintain their attacking threat while managing minutes across the squad.

item.title: Five losses: Michael Carrick must finally put an end to haunting Daniel Farke statistic vs Leeds
item.description: Five losses: Michael Carrick must finally put an end to haunting Daniel Farke statistic vs Leeds Michael Carrick will be looking to get one over on Daniel Farke for the first time as a manager tomorrow. Manchester United make the trip to Yorkshire to lock horns with arch-rivals Leeds United in a 2pm kick-off. How has Carrick fared against Farke? (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) In the meantime, Opta has shared a hugely concerning statistic that the Old Trafford faithful will be hoping comes to an end at Elland Road. Since taking the leap into managerial roles, Carrick has lost all five league games in which he’s come up against Farke. Farke has dealt the United boss his most defeats, so the unwanted feat will undoubtedly be at the back of Carrick’s mind when he takes to the dugout on Sunday. 5 – Michael Carrick has lost all five of his managerial league meetings with Daniel Farke, suffering his most defeats as a manager to the current Leeds United boss. Showdown. pic.twitter.com/o6FF7svrKM It’s safe to say that a win is also imperative for the former Red, with his tenure already being tipped for a premature end due to United’s dismal start to the campaign. What has Farke had to say about under-pressure Carrick? (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Across their opening nine matches in all competitions, United have been on winning side only twice, against newly-promoted Ipswich Town in the Premier League on August 30 and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah in their Champions League opener on September 10. They have drawn against Everton, Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur, while losing to Hull City, Manchester City and, on Tuesday, Atletico Madrid. Remarkably, Falke actually took the time to rally behind Carrick in his pre-game press conference on Friday, saying: “We don’t have many young British coaches in the Premier League. We have a promising one, who has done excellent jobs at Middlesbrough and when [he] came in at Manchester United to steady the ship. “But after six games, when they haven’t had a horrendous start — okay, by their perception [they have], as they want to challenge for the title. The criticism has started already. I don’t like it. If we have young promising managers, let’s look after them, especially when you look at what he’s done for the club over many years as a player and a coach in a very difficult situation. He did a tremendous job. “We should back young British managers. Yes, I have a German passport, but I’m not too far away from getting British status. I like it when young British managers come through. The outside world wants to see everyone fail. We should be happy to have someone with so much potential and not question them too early.” Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.title: CSD consider sanctioning Javier Tebas for ‘Nazi’ comparisons of Real Madrid – report
item.description: CSD consider sanctioning Javier Tebas for ‘Nazi’ comparisons of Real Madrid – report Tensions between Real Madrid and La Liga are at an all-time high, with Javier Tebas leading the line for the league and coming heavily under fire in recent days. The recent outburst began when Tebas compared Real Madrid TV’s comments and telecasts to the propaganda of Nazi Germany , clearly crossing a line in the process. “ Real Madrid TV leads the way. The score is always the same: select the incidents that suit their interests, repeat the grievance, fuel suspicion and identify the enemies.” “This method recalls propaganda techniques exploited by Goebbels, the propaganda minister of Nazi Germany: systematic repetition, the creation of an enemy and the subordination of facts to a narrative,” he added. The comments, needless to say, riled up the Real Madrid offices, who immediately hit out and called for Tebas’ resignation as the president of La Liga. Sanctions being studied Florentino Perez has called for Tebas’ resignation. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Now, as reported by MARCA in a recent update, the Superior Council for Sports (CSD) is studying acting ex officio in the Real Madrid-Tebas issue and handing the league president a possible sanction. The development comes as a big win for Real Madrid, who will finally feel their voice is being deservedly heard. After all, having a league president who openly compares one of the biggest clubs in the league to Nazi Germany comes as a new low for La Liga. As matters stand, however, the CSD is only looking into the matter and has yet to decide whether Real Madrid’s calls for Tebas’ resignation have enough merit. In any case, the league president must not get away easily with such a disgraceful statement. Real Madrid’s accusations Tebas likened Real Madrid TV to ‘Nazi propoganda’. (Photo by Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images For Sportel) Through their long official communication on the matter, Real Madrid hit out elaborately at Tebas and placed several accusations at him. For starters, they addressed the elephant in the room – the comparison to Nazi Germany and how it was very distasteful and disrespectful to do so. The club, however, went on and highlighted that this is not the first time Tebas has spoken negatively about Real Madrid, especially when the club are also on the right side of the Negreira scandal. Concurrently, the club also called for a better refereeing system with a complete revamp and stated how Tebas and Co. have been unresponsive on the Negreira matter despite knowing how serious the accusation is. They particularly called out the president for his lack of neutrality, respect, and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities, thus calling for his resignation.

item.title: Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer fires back at Mike Tomlin’s ‘dead’ take about Dallas’ player only meeting
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer fires back at Mike Tomlin’s ‘dead’ take about Dallas’ player only meeting appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys ’ defense has drawn plenty of criticism this season, and a players-only meeting added to the noise . Brian Schottenheimer is not buying the idea that the gathering is a bad sign. Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin made waves earlier this week when he weighed in on the Cowboys’ defensive meeting on the New Heights podcast . Tomlin’s verdict on teams that hold players-only meetings was blunt. “I think you’re dead,” Tomlin said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Schottenheimer offered a different view when asked about it on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, according to Jon Machota of The Athletic. “I think they’re very, very different. I’ve been around the league a long time. I have great respect for Mike. It depends on the type of meeting,” Schottenheimer said. “If you go into a meeting and the players-only meeting is a b**** session, I don’t think that that’s a good thing. Matter of fact, I know it’s not a good thing.” The Cowboys head coach pointed to the leadership behind this particular meeting as the difference. “But when you’ve got leaders like Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark and guys like that that are driving the meeting with a purpose and they’re talking about the things they talked about in that meeting, I don’t think that’s a bad thing,” Schottenheimer said. “I think it shows ownership on their part.” “Their pride is real. They want to be great. They want to win,” Schottenheimer said. “I certainly wasn’t in the meeting, but I’ve talked to the guys that kind of led it, and it sounds like it was a very, very productive meeting with solution-oriented conversations.” The meeting followed a 24-16 home loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers that dropped Dallas to 2-3. The defense has been a major problem, allowing 395.4 yards per game, the second-most in the NFL. Williams has taken the blame publicly, saying he takes “full accountability and full responsibility for the way this defense is going at the moment.” He declined to share details about what was said, telling reporters he was going to keep that to himself. Dallas will get a chance to show whether the meeting made a difference on Sunday night, when the Cowboys visit the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field . Related: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones drops defiantly confident take about 2026 season despite rocky start Related: Cowboys’ Mike Pettine reveals true role on coaching staff for gamedays

item.title: Fresh Celtic Injury Concern Raised After Loss vs Benfica
item.description: Some time has passed and the dust has now settled on Celtic 's defeat away in Portugal at the hands of Benfica . The result means that the Hoops have started off their Europa League campaign with two defeats. That is far from ideal. Celtic do not have much time to dwell on the result though, as the games keep coming thick and fast. Their next one is against Hearts at the weekend. Celtic must keep winning in the league as the Rangers have found some form and are cranking up the pressure on Martin O'Neill's side. So, the Hoops would like to have their best players available moving forward. But there is some concern about the fitness status of one key player going into the game against Hearts. Is Celtic player carrying a knock? When the lineup against Benfica came out, there was one clear surprise. Liam Scales had been left on the bench in favour of a starting centre-back duo of Dane Murray and Auston Trusty. It was a curious decision, to say the least. Murray simply does not have the experience at this level and has often faced criticism from the fans for some of his performances this season. It would be safe to say that it did not work as well as O'Neill would have hoped for. After all, Celtic did end up conceding four goals, and it could have been more. As for Scales, could the Irishman have been carrying some sort of knock, which played a factor in O'Neill's decision-making against Benfica? As reported by CeltsAreHere , Charlie Mulgrew said while speaking on Premier Sports Ireland: “Scales, you can only assume he’s got a knock and is being rested. Because I think you see how big a player he is for Celtic. It’s not always appreciated but he is somebody who heads the ball in the box and defends well.” Everton Insider Makes Major David Moyes to Celtic Claim The Everton insider has shared his view on the recent links involving David Moyes and Celtic. Celtic need players like Liam Scales right now Celtic certainly appeared to miss Scales against Benfica. At times, it felt that they were too easy to open up for the hosts. Despite that, O'Neill did not bring on Scales and kept him on the bench as an unused substitute. Nothing has come out since then that would suggest that Scales is injured, which should raise a few more eyebrows about the decisions from O'Neill against Benfica. It remains to be seen if Scales will be involved against Hearts at the weekend or not. To be honest, it does feel like Celtic could do with experience and leadership at the back at this point in time, as they try to get past a rough patch of form. They have lost four of their last five games across all competitions. There is little room for error moving forward. If the results do not improve, they might have little choice but to part ways with O'Neill.

item.title: ‘I Ain’t Really See Nothing Wrong With It’ — Super Bowl Champion Pushes Back Against Criticism of Packers Star Micah Parsons’ Podcast
item.description: ‘I Ain’t Really See Nothing Wrong With It’ — Super Bowl Champion Pushes Back Against Criticism of Packers Star Micah Parsons’ Podcast In recent years, more athletes have jumped into the media world by launching their own podcasts. While many wait until their playing careers are over, Micah Parsons wasted little time, launching his show before his rookie contract had even ended. But getting into the podcast game early hasn’t come without its share of controversy. Parsons’ willingness to speak his mind about fellow players and teams has earned him plenty of criticism. Now, the Green Bay Packers star has someone in his corner, with former Super Bowl champion Aqib Talib pushing back against the backlash. Aqib Talib Defends Micah Parsons’ Podcast Parsons launched “The EDGE” more than three years ago, giving him a platform to share his unfiltered opinions on the NFL. His approach has not always gone over well, drawing pushback from former players, media analysts, and even a teammate . Critics have even questioned whether the podcast distracts him from football, while others have objected to his comments about fellow NFL players. Talib, however, sees little reason for concern. The former Denver Broncos cornerback joined “NFL on FOX” as an analyst after retiring and now hosts a podcast with Skip Bayless called “The Gridiron.” During a recent segment on the show, Talib explained why he believes Parsons is simply taking advantage of the platform available to him. “I ain’t really see nothing wrong with it either. It’s a new day and age, bro. These guys got platforms, you know what I’m saying? This is what they do,” Talib said . The Super Bowl winner also pointed to players such as Caleb Downs and Amon-Ra St. Brown, who have embraced the media space, arguing that podcasts have become a natural part of the modern sports landscape. Ain’t no point in beating around the bush and saying [expletive] on it. You feel me? You might as well speak your mind. Get your subs up,” he said. Parsons faced his strongest backlash after criticizing Jayden Daniels following the Washington Commanders’ overtime tie with the New York Giants. The Packers star took issue with Daniels’ lack of urgency in the closing seconds, arguing that his decisions cost Washington a chance to score. It’s a new day and age, bro. These guys got platforms, you know what I’m saying? This is what they do,” Talib said . The Super Bowl winner also pointed to players such as Caleb Downs and Amon-Ra St. Brown, who have embraced the media space, arguing that podcasts have become a natural part of the modern sports landscape. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “It’s a new day and age, man. And if you’re going to have a podcast, you might as well speak your mind. Ain’t no point in beating around the bush and saying [expletive] on it. You feel me? You might as well speak your mind. Get your subs up,” he said. Parsons faced his strongest backlash after criticizing Jayden Daniels following the Washington Commanders’ overtime tie with the New York Giants. The Packers star took issue with Daniels’ lack of urgency in the closing seconds, arguing that his decisions cost Washington a chance to score. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer With 12 seconds left and no timeouts, Daniels took a sack instead of getting rid of the ball, and Washington could not get lined up to spike it before time expired. Parsons argued that the quarterback’s failure to recognize the urgency of the situation left the Commanders empty-handed in Week 5. “Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job, to be honest with you. To be honest with you. And, like, I’m a big Jayden Daniels fan. But the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend,” Parsons said. “Respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that, like, I’m a defensive player, and this [expletive] is programmed into me. I know what to do in those situations. There’s no way I’m taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. “Mind you, it’d be different if Jayden Daniels were a rookie. This is your third year. This your third year. You’ve been to the NFC Championship Game. You’ve been in big moments before. And to me, even after a sack, you’re casually getting up.” Whether Talib’s support and that of others will encourage Parsons to stick with his unfiltered style remains to be seen. The criticism could also prompt him to rethink his approach in the coming weeks. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Watch Lakers’ Luka Doncic power through Nikola Jokic for tough and-1
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Watch Lakers’ Luka Doncic power through Nikola Jokic for tough and-1 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic reminded everyone why he remains one of the NBA’s most difficult players to contain . He powered through Nikola Jokic for a tough and-1 in the Los Angeles Lakers ’ preseason finale against the Denver Nuggets on Friday night. During the second quarter at Crypto.com Arena, Doncic attacked downhill and drove directly into the chest of the three-time MVP. Despite absorbing heavy contact from Denver’s imposing center, the Lakers superstar maintained his balance, flipped a contested shot off the glass, and drew the foul to complete an emphatic three-point play . Luka Doncic goes into the body of Nikola Jokic for the and-1 😤 pic.twitter.com/oiDlEaJNNu Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 17, 2026 The sequence offered a glimpse of Doncic’s physical readiness heading into the 2026–27 campaign, even as Los Angeles fell 121-106. Doncic finished with 15 points, four rebounds, and three three-pointers in 19 minutes. He shot 4-of-8 from the field. Jokic countered with 17 points, six rebounds, and eight assists on 7-of-8 shooting. Meanwhile, Jamal Murray paced Denver with 21 points. Austin Reaves led the Lakers with 19 points. With the exhibition schedule complete, Los Angeles now turns its attention to Wednesday’s regular-season opener against the Golden State Warriors. Doncic has looked sharp throughout the 2026 preseason. He continues to be the centerpiece of head coach JJ Redick’s offense while the Lakers carefully managed his minutes. Doncic opened the exhibition slate with 21 points against Sacramento before adding 23 in the rematch. He then capped his preparation with Friday’s efficient performance against Denver. More importantly, his ability to create scoring opportunities through contact reinforced the physical edge that makes him such a difficult matchup. With Reaves providing another scoring option and Walker Kessler strengthening the interior, Doncic and the Lakers have plenty of reasons for optimism. Related: JJ Redick drops brutally honest truth bomb on Dalton Knecht Related: Lakers hopeful gets candid about final roster chances

Luka Doncic goes into the body of Nikola Jokic for the and-1 😤 pic.twitter.com/oiDlEaJNNu Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 17, 2026 The sequence offered a glimpse of Doncic’s physical readiness heading into the 2026–27 campaign, even as Los Angeles fell 121-106. Doncic finished with 15 points, four rebounds, and three three-pointers in 19 minutes. He shot 4-of-8 from the field. Jokic countered with 17 points, six rebounds, and eight assists on 7-of-8 shooting. Meanwhile, Jamal Murray paced Denver with 21 points. Austin Reaves led the Lakers with 19 points. With the exhibition schedule complete, Los Angeles now turns its attention to Wednesday’s regular-season opener against the Golden State Warriors. Doncic has looked sharp throughout the 2026 preseason. He continues to be the centerpiece of head coach JJ Redick’s offense while the Lakers carefully managed his minutes. Doncic opened the exhibition slate with 21 points against Sacramento before adding 23 in the rematch. He then capped his preparation with Friday’s efficient performance against Denver. More importantly, his ability to create scoring opportunities through contact reinforced the physical edge that makes him such a difficult matchup. With Reaves providing another scoring option and Walker Kessler strengthening the interior, Doncic and the Lakers have plenty of reasons for optimism. item.title: Warriors reportedly waiving ex-76ers 6-foot-6 wing, former first-round pick after preseason
item.description: Warriors reportedly waiving ex-76ers 6-foot-6 wing, former first-round pick after preseason originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors spent much of the summer trying to piece together their roster after missing out on LeBron James and Anthony Davis. They ultimately assembled a roster with enough depth to help support Steph Curry and Draymond Green. One of the additions was former first-round pick Dalen Terry, whom Golden State signed to a non-guaranteed deal. “The Golden State Warriors and Dalen Terry have agreed to a deal, league sources told hoopshype. Terry, the 18th pick of the 2022 NBA Draft, has played four combined NBA seasons with the Chicago Bulls and Philadelphia 76ers ,” HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto wrote. Terry was originally drafted by the Chicago Bulls before joining the Philadelphia 76ers in February of last season. Philadelphia looked to develop him, but the organization eventually needed to clear roster space for LeBron James and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. “The Sixers waive Dalen Terry to clear space for LeBron James and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Terry, a former first-round pick, had a non-guaranteed contract for the upcoming season. Philadelphia must still move one additional player to create enough room for both additions,” NBA writer Jake Weinbach wrote. With the regular season approaching, the Warriors need to finalize their 15-man roster. Terry will be one of the players affected by those roster decisions. “The Warriors are planning on waiving Dalen Terry before Monday and having him join the Santa Cruz Warriors, sources told ClutchPoints. Terry is a player the Warriors like and will continue developing in the G League. Tonight is the team's final preseason game against POR,” NBA insider Brett Siegel posted. The positive for Terry is that Golden State still sees potential in him and wants to continue developing him. The Warriors are giving him an opportunity to improve in the G League, but he will need to make the most of that chance if he hopes to return to the NBA. This does not have to be the end of Terry's NBA aspirations. He can continue working on his game with the Santa Cruz Warriors and try to earn another opportunity at the highest level. For now, however, his path back to the NBA will likely begin in the G League. You a b**, yeah you heard me, You a b****,” Haliburton appeared to repeat toward Rollins. Both players received technical fouls following the confrontation. Friday’s matchup represented another opportunity to regain his rhythm before the regular season. Yet there was nothing cautious about his reaction to Rollins. Even in preseason action, the All-Star guard clearly wasn’t interested in allowing an opponent to push him around. item.title: “I Need Him to Get His Opportunity”: 5x Grammy Winner Sends Clear Message to Browns Over Shedeur Sanders
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA – AUGUST 16: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders 12 is shown after the preseason game between the Cleveland Browns and the Philadelphia Eagles on August 16th, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA AUG 16 Preseason Browns at Eagles EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon250816131 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Lil Wayne wants the Cleveland Browns to have a quarterback headache, just not the kind that comes from another loss. The five-time Grammy winner would rather see the franchise wrestling with a difficult decision about Shedeur Sanders than reach the end of the season without knowing what Sanders can offer. Speaking [on [Gridiron](](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vidtHqKSMnk), co-hosted by Skip Bayless and Aqib Talib, during a conversation previewing the Packers-Cowboys matchup, Bayless asked Lil Wayne whether he wanted Sanders playing somewhere other than Cleveland. “I need him to get his opportunity, and I think where he at he’s going to get that opportunity,” Wayne said on the show. That distinction matters because Sanders is not currently Cleveland’s starter. The Browns’ official depth chart lists Deshaun Watson first and Sanders second, and the team has continued with Watson despite the attention surrounding him. Cleveland’s decision to start Watson was made after evaluating the offseason, training camp, and preseason, rather than treating the competition as a week-to-week contest. A major voice is demanding the Browns give Shedeur Sanders his shot. Subscribe to stay on top of the QB competition heating up in Cleveland. Head coach Todd Monken explained the decision in August, saying: “We felt over the course of training camp and the offseason that (Watson) was ahead of Shedeur,” Monken said. “Shedeur’s closed that gap, for sure. And that’s a credit to him. We look forward to Shedeur continuing to grow as a player, but ultimately, we’re about Week 1. Putting our best foot forward over the next three weeks.” “Ultimately we expect him to play well or we wouldn’t be starting him,” he said. Cleveland entered Week 6 with a 3-2 record after losing 17-12 to the New York Jets on October 11. Watson threw for 155 yards and was sacked eight times in that defeat, while a botched punt snap also hurt the Browns late in the game. The loss does not, by itself, mean Sanders should take over, but it gives the team another performance to evaluate as it weighs what it needs from its offense. Watson has given Cleveland reasons to stick with him, but the numbers have hardly made the decision foolproof. Then came the Jets game: just 155 passing yards, eight sacks, and a 17-12 loss. Wayne, however, was not calling for Watson to be benched or suggesting Sanders had already earned the starting job. In fact, he made a point of saying he was happy to see Watson playing well earlier in the season. “But I love to see Deshaun doing his thing now. I love that. I want Deshaun to give them a problem. item.title: 😵‍💫 Homebody syndrome hits: Can this star only shine in the Bundesliga?
item.description: 😵‍💫 Homebody syndrome hits: Can this star only shine in the Bundesliga? For three years, Christopher Nkunku had been searching for his old self. At Chelsea? He had terrible luck with injuries. At Milan? He did a solid job, but nothing more. Only now, back in Leipzig, is the Frenchman really turning on the style again. Last weekend, he even scored a hat-trick in the 6–0 rout of a helpless Frankfurt side—a “perfect” one by Germany’s strict definition: three consecutive goals in a single half. It was the first in the Red Bulls’ ten-year Bundesliga history. So is Nkunku a classic case of someone who can only do his business at home? It’s not quite that simple. But there are good reasons why the attacking star has rediscovered his explosive form in Saxony, of all places. Finally fit instead of constantly injured When Chelsea splashed out around €60 million on Nkunku in the summer of 2023, expectations were enormous. After all, the technically gifted forward arrived in England as the newly crowned Bundesliga top scorer and Player of the Season. But injuries repeatedly set him back. 📸 RONNY HARTMANN - AFP or licensors The 28-year-old never really found a consistent rhythm at Milan last season either. In Leipzig, they know his injury history. But they also know exactly how good Nkunku can be when his body cooperates. There’s a reason he racked up an impressive 70 goals and 56 assists in 172 competitive appearances across all competitions during his first spell at RB. That talent obviously hasn’t simply vanished. Rather, Nkunku first had to lay the groundwork to be able to deliver consistently again. Probably the most important factor in that respect was his decision not to spend the three-week international break putting his feet up. Lacking fitness after being demoted in Milan, he worked with a personal trainer in Leipzig and then trained at RB too. "I knew I had to work on my physical problems, and that’s what I tried to do during the international break," he explained, drawing a clear conclusion: "I think that was a good decision." "A massive asset" But an attacking focal point like Nkunku needs more than just the legs for the job—he also needs a role that suits him. Under Martín Demichelis, the 18-cap international plays behind centre-forward Rômulo, where he can put his strengths to good use. He moves between the lines, links up with teammates and bursts into the box at just the right moment. ADVERTISEMENT: Will Leipzig get steamrollered by Bayern? Captain David Raum also stresses: "When he gets going, he’s a massive asset for us." Sounds like an environment that knows exactly what it has in its returning star. item.title: Liverpool suffer massive blow in race for next £100m signing
item.description: Liverpool suffer massive blow in race for next £100m signing Since Mohamed Salah announced that he would be departing Liverpool, there has been plenty of discussion over who could replace him. The Egyptian King left Anfield over three months ago, and it still isn’t clear who the club view as his successor. Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola were both added in the summer, but neither is a clear natural fit in Salah’s old position. Rio Ngumoha has been relied upon on the right-wing at times this campaign, but again he isn’t a long-term solution. Liverpool may need to turn to the transfer market again to replace Salah, but they have just received a big blow in the pursuit of their best option. Liverpool told top target prefers move to Spain Michael Olise has long been considered the absolute premier option when it comes to replacing Salah. The French international has been a revelation for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga and has forced his way into the Ballon d’Or discussion since his move from Crystal Palace. For some time it felt as though Olise to Liverpool was inevitable, but now the forward may favour a move elsewhere. That’s according to German football insider Christian Falk , who claims that Olise now favours a move to Spain over a return to England if he were to leave Bavaria. Falk confirmed that a move back to the Premier League isn’t impossible, with several clubs in the division being ‘very interesting’ for Olise, but that Real Madrid are the team that excites the 24-year-old the most. Olise produced 22 goals and 31 assists for Bayern last season and already has 12 goal involvements in nine matches this campaign, truly world class output. Liverpool signing Olise would be the final piece in a long and expensive overhaul of the attack but would also instantly make the Reds challengers for every trophy available to them. The challenge remains convincing the French international to move to Merseyside over Madrid, but with an already star-studded forward line the club will surely be able to make a convincing pitch. A move for Olise won’t be straightforward, but is the absolute dream for many of the Anfield faithful, and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Julian Ward and co try and convince the Frenchman to join England’s most successful club.

item.title: PAC’s sudden death explained as official cause emerges weeks after AEW star’s passing
item.description: Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images The official cause of death of AEW star PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, has been revealed weeks after his sudden passing at the age of 40. According to a report from the New York Post, the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office determined that the British wrestler died from bronchial asthma. His death was ruled natural. PAC’s passing shocked the wrestling world after he competed at AEW All Out in Chicago on September 26, with reports stating he was found unconscious in a rental car the following day. Medical examiner confirms bronchial asthma caused PAC’s death A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office told the California Post that investigators had determined the cause of PAC’s death following an investigation. “Officials have determined what killed wrestling star Benjamin Satterley. A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office told the California Post on Monday that following a probe into his sudden death, investigators concluded Satterley — who performed in AEW rings as “Pac” — passed away from bronchial asthma. “The manner of his death was officially ruled natural, the rep added. Satterley was discovered unconscious in a rental car outside of a CAVA in Des Plaines, Ill. at around 4 p.m. on Sept. 27.” The revelation offers an explanation for the sudden loss of a wrestler who remained active in the ring shortly before his death. PAC had reportedly pulled over in a car park before being discovered unconscious. However, all the available reports do not provide further details about the medical emergency. The wrestling world has continued to pay tribute to the former WWE star, who competed under the name Neville during his time with the company. AEW held a tribute to honour PAC’s life, while several of his peers also shared emotional memories of the wrestler. Names including Jon Moxley, Kevin Owens, Cody Rhodes and Bryan Danielson were among those reported to have spoken about his impact. PAC built a reputation as one of wrestling’s most exciting performers, known for his high-flying style and work across WWE and AEW. His cause of death has now been officially established, but the loss continues to be felt by fans and colleagues who followed his career. item.title: Aston Villa XI vs Newcastle United – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Aston Villa XI vs Newcastle United – Predicted lineup and team news Aston Villa visit Newcastle United on Saturday evening on five points from six league games, with Unai Emery chasing his 100th Premier League win. Villa beat Fenerbahce 6-0 in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both scoring twice. They have scored at least three goals in four of their last six games in all competitions. Villa drew 2-2 at home to Brentford in their previous league game and have won three and drawn one of their last four away games. Only three of their last 10 meetings with Newcastle in all competitions have ended in Villa wins. Aston Villa team news Ian Maatsen (ankle), Amadou Onana (knee), Matteo Ruggeri (thigh) and Modou Keba Cisse are listed as out, although Emery said earlier this week that Maatsen is close to returning. George Hemmings (knee) and Brian Madjo (ankle) are doubtful, with Emery having said earlier this week that both could return. Leon Goretzka made his debut as a substitute against Fenerbahce but is unlikely to start. Joao Gomes is expected to return alongside Boubacar Kamara in central midfield, with Emiliano Buendia likely to replace Barkley, who scored twice in midweek. Captain John McGinn and Johan Manzambi are the most likely pair out wide, with Ibrahim Mbaye dropping to the bench. Nicolas Jackson, who has scored four goals in his last three appearances, is expected to lead the line. Aaron Wan-Bissaka may again cover at left-back, with Matty Cash on the right, Victor Lindelof and Pau Torres at centre-back and Zion Suzuki in goal. Aston Villa predicted lineup Aston Villa possible starting XI: Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Wan-Bissaka; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Manzambi; Jackson When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 17:30 BST on Saturday, 17 October 2026. How to watch Newcastle United vs Aston Villa? The match will be broadcast live in the UK on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League. item.title: Palisades defeats Hamilton in Western League showdown
item.description: Jameson Della Bella runs for the first of his two touchdowns in a win over Hamilton on Friday night. (Steve Galluzzo / For The Times) Jameson Della Bella ran for 86 yards and two touchdowns while Robert Holohan ran for a touchdown and threw for one more as Palisades dominated Hamilton 35-18 Friday night in a Western League showdown. The Dolphins’ defense was up to the task against Hamilton’s highly touted quarterback Thaddeus Breaux, intercepting two of his passes and sacking him four times. “It was fourth down, we had to make something happen, I saw him throw and I just ran full speed and dove for it,” said safety Aidan Wilson-Turner, who picked off a pass over the middle at Palisades’ 18-yard line to keep the Yankees off the scoreboard late in the first half. Breaux, a sophomore who has received a scholarship offer from UCLA, threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns in last year’s 46-30 loss to Palisades but was 27–of-44 passing for 217 yards Friday — most of that yardage in the fourth quarter with the outcome long decided. He threw scoring passes of eight, 11 and four yards. “The defensive line did a great job putting pressure on him,” Wilson-Turner added. “Our job in the secondary was to stay deep, playoff off them and stay true to our zones.” Palisades (4-3, 3-0) took a major step toward defending the league title with only games at fifth-place Fairfax and at home versus last-place Westchester remaining. Thaddeus Breaux threw for three touchdowns in Friday's loss at Palisades. (Steve Galluzzo / For The Times) Hamilton, which fell to 3-5, 2-1, last won the league in 2014. Della Bella’s six-yard run gave Palisades a 21-0 lead midway through the second quarter and the Dolphins increased their advantage to 35-0 early in the third quarter on Holohan’s 13-yard pass to Go Moriya and his four-yard quarterback keeper. item.title: “She hasn’t done this alone” – Linda Cohn Makes Brutal Angel Reese Claim as ‘Caitlin Clark Effect’ Comparisons Intensify
item.description: Angel Reese, Caitlin Clark - Image © Imagn Images It’s been a while since the Angel Reese vs. Caitlin Clark narrative has commanded the spotlight. On Friday, WNBA analyst Linda Cohn reminded fans of this plotline. In the latest edition of “The Linda Cohn Show,” Cohn acknowledged Reese’s rising prominence and said some fans were likening her popularity to Clark’s. “Angel Reese, as we all know, has become one of the biggest names in the WNBA. She’s helping bring attention to the Atlanta Dream…Now, Atlanta has other outstanding players. She hasn’t done this alone. Rhyne Howard, Jordin Canada, Allisha Gray, if she’s healthy enough to play…Here’s where I think the conversation is getting ahead of itself, and it’s worth repeating. People are already trying to compare the Angel Reese effect with the Caitlin Clark effect.” According to Cohn, a genuine comparison can only be made by looking at the numbers drawn by the two WNBA All-Stars. “Angel Reese absolutely has her own following and her own impact on the sport. But if we’re gonna make comparisons about who’s driving ticket sales, let’s compare actual ticket sales. Let’s compare attendance. Let’s compare consistent demand over an entire season, not just a couple of Finals games.” Clark has downplayed suggestions of animosity toward Reese. She told off a reporter at the FIBA World Cup for asking whether she and Reese are “friends now.” “I’m Not Going to Shy Away From This Moment”: Angel Reese Opens Up on Her Mindset Heading Into WNBA Finals From the looks of it, Angel Reese isn’t focused on a popularity contest, either. On Friday’s edition of “NBA Today,” ESPN’s Kendra Andrews shared some quotes from her conversation with the Dream star ahead of her first-ever WNBA Finals appearance. “She said, ‘To be a good player in the playoffs, you have to just elevate. You have to be someone who rises. The best players are the ones who are the greats, the ones that get the most respect, the ones that deliver on this level. I’m not going to shy away from this moment.'” Reese is known to elevate her game in crunch situations, helping the LSU Tigers win the 2023 national championship. Now, her mettle will be tested again as the Dream take on the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals. item.title: Nolan Lashley is Republic football's new touchdown king
item.description: REPUBLIC — If you lose concentration during a Republic football game, you’ve probably missed a Nolan Lashley touchdown. The junior running back is finding the end zone early and often. Defenses can’t slow him down, while his offensive line is generating holes big enough for an SUV to drive through. No. 3 Republic (7-1) notched its biggest win of the season on Friday, Oct. 16, toppling Carthage 26-22 thanks to three rushing touchdowns from Lashley. Week 8: Breaking down Springfield-area high school football action Lashley has now scored 27 touchdowns this season, breaking the school record for most touchdowns in a season. Jerney Jones held the previous record with 26 touchdowns in 2015. Southwest Missouri has been a hotbed of great running backs. The best teams rely on their backs to win games. Republic is no different through Lashley. Lashley has seen his peers' success around the region. It has only made him hungrier, he told the News-Leader last week. “It makes me want to compete more,” Lashley said. “When I go and look at stats, I see that I’m not leading in yards. It makes me want to compete. I want to be No. 1 in everything.” More Nolan Lashley: What's it like to block for Republic football's Nolan Lashley? Lashley will forever be known as Republic’s touchdown king. Head coach Ryan Cornelsen says his willingness to deliver hits and be fearless sets him apart from the rest. “He takes a pounding, no doubt,” Cornelsen said. “Running the ball in our offense is not for the faint of heart. He takes pride in that and does a good job.” The Tigers will face Willard (1-7) next week to close out the regular season. With expectations of a deep postseason run, Republic will continue to rely on Lashley. The touchdown record will keep moving, just like Lashley’s legs in every pile. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. Send stats or information to him at Lkeating@usatodayco.com This article originally appeared on Springfield News-Leader: Nolan Lashley is Republic football's new touchdown king

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: The Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool?
item.description: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In the Champions League rout of Lask he was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In the previous game against Manchester City , however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. It also did not help his cause that Rayan Cherki, a cheaper alternative whom Liverpool considered and passed on, completed City’s victory with a sublime goal. AH Continue reading...

item.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga president resign over Goebbels comparison
item.description: Javier Tebas accuses Madrid of ‘propaganda techniques’ Club want ‘immediate resignation’ for ‘constant attacks’ Real Madrid have again demanded the resignation of the president of La Liga after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of Nazi Germany. Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticised how its club television channel says referees hurt its chances of winning. The channel regularly runs reels of what it considers gross errors by match officials who are set to work upcoming games for the 15-time European champions. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.description: Spanish head coach will be under huge pressure if he comes unstuck again at home to Hull on Saturday Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions. Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices. Continue reading...

The Guardian has learned that several council members demanded the award be abolished and others called for the prize to be depoliticised, with Fifa’s football social responsibility committee to make a recommendation before the next council meeting in Doha on 16 December. item.title: Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?
item.description: Pundits regularly criticise teams for not running enough but is there a link between distance covered and results? By Opta Analyst It was like clockwork. Manchester United dropped points against Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical statistics to make points. Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Manchester United.” Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Henderson back on Merseyside, Farke threatens more misery for Carrick and Forest are a threat to Arsenal Premier League top scorers | Follow us on TikTok A lively reception awaits the former Liverpool midfielders Jordan Henderson and Xabi Alonso at Everton and, in the case of the former, any jeers can be considered an unintentional tribute. They will speak of what the 36-year-old is able to produce now as much as what, and where, he delivered in the past. With two goals and an assist against Bournemouth last Saturday, Henderson became the oldest player to contribute directly to three goals in a Premier League game, and demonstrated his role at Chelsea is not simply to elevate standards off the pitch. His midfield partnership with Moisés Caicedo gave Alonso’s team balance and enabled the front three of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer to flourish. Their confrontation against an Everton defence that had impressed this season, only to litter the draw at Hull with costly mistakes, will provide a stern test of the hosts’ unbeaten start and may well be dictated by the veteran behind them. item.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
item.description: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations. Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

item.title: Europa League: Lyon take down Crystal Palace as Benfica overwhelm Celtic
item.description: Sage loses 3-2 to former side; Benfica 4-1 Celtic Juventus go top with 2-1 win over Celta Vigo Pierre Sage endured a frustrating return to Lyon in the Europa League as his Crystal Palace side lost 3-2 to his former employers at the Groupama Stadium. Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half without a shot on target for the visitors. Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s two-goal advantage. The Palace substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find an equaliser. Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea are the Premier League’s most fun team but is it sustainable?
item.description: Xabi Alonso’s side are scoring and conceding at a remarkable rate. It’s great for neutrals but not necessarily the best way to qualify for Europe By WhoScored Watching Chelsea this season ought to come with a health warning. Goals arrive in abundance, leads are established before spectators have settled into their seats and clean sheets have become an alien concept. Xabi Alonso has transformed Chelsea into one of the Premier League’s most thrilling spectacles. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 13. That’s 4.7 goals per game in six matches. Chelsea are a neutral’s dream, but is it sustainable? They have scored 15 goals from an expected goals total of just 8.4, an over-performance of 6.6. Their 18.3% conversion rate is second only to Manchester City’s 19.1%, while eight of their 15 goals have come from shots with xG below 0.13. The five goals against Bournemouth last weekend came from an xG of just 0.75. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...

item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. John Brewin Match report: Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City Match report: Crystal Palace 3-1 Nottingham Forest Match report: Hull City 2-2 Everton Continue reading...

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
item.description: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. It was an amazing way to go out on a high.” Five months later McKenna has no regrets about electing to cut things short while the going was so good. The golf bag lying outside his garage speaks of a man enjoying the break and, more pertinently, of something bigger. His son has recently become interested in the sport and sharing those moments with loved ones, whether out on the greens or spending part of the summer travelling along the East Anglian coastline in a camper van, were among the biggest reasons to pause a soaring career. At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
